{{Short description|American actor and writer (born 1943)}} {{distinguish|Shaun Wallace}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox person | name = Wallace Shawn | image = Wallace Shawn Jay Kelly-37 (cropped).jpg | caption = Shawn in 2025 | other_names = | birth_name = Wallace Michael Shawn | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1943|11|12}} | birth_place = [[New York City]], U.S. | education = [[Harvard University]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|AB]])
[[Magdalen College, Oxford]] | occupation = {{hlist|Actor|essayist|writer}} | years_active = 1965–present | notable_works = [[Wallace Shawn on screen and stage]] | partner = [[Deborah Eisenberg]] (1972–present) | father = [[William Shawn]] | relatives = [[Allen Shawn]] (brother) }} '''Wallace Michael Shawn''' (born November 12, 1943){{Cite web|last=Reeves|first=Dan|url=https://nsjonline.com/article/2025/11/famous-birthdays-this-week-nov-6-to-nov-12/|title=Famous birthdays this week: Nov. 6 to Nov. 12|work=[[North State Journal]]|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2026|archive-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213075020/https://nsjonline.com/article/2025/11/famous-birthdays-this-week-nov-6-to-nov-12/|url-status=live}} is an American actor, essayist, and writer. He is known for playing Vizzini in ''[[The Princess Bride]]'' (1987), Mr. Hall in ''[[Clueless]]'' (1995), and Dr. John Sturgis in ''[[Young Sheldon]]'' (2017–2024), and for voicing [[List of Toy Story characters#Rex|Rex the Dinosaur]] in the [[Toy Story (franchise)|''Toy Story'' franchise]] (1995–2026). Shawn also appeared in ''[[The Bostonians (film)|The Bostonians]]'' (1984), ''[[Prick Up Your Ears]]'' (1987), ''[[Scenes from the Class Struggle in Beverly Hills]]'' (1989), ''[[Vanya on 42nd Street]]'' (1994), ''[[The Haunted Mansion (2003 film)|The Haunted Mansion]]'' (2003), ''[[The Incredibles]]'' (2004), ''[[Southland Tales]]'' (2006), ''[[The Double (2013 film)|The Double]]'' (2013), and ''[[Marriage Story]]'' (2019). He appeared in six [[Woody Allen]] films including ''[[Manhattan (1979 film)|Manhattan]]'' (1979), ''[[Radio Days]]'' (1987), and ''[[Rifkin's Festival]]'' (2020). His television work includes recurring roles as Arnie Ross in ''Taxi'' (1978-1983), Jeff Engels in ''[[The Cosby Show]]'' (1987–1991), [[Grand Nagus Zek]] in ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' (1993–1999), Cyrus Rose in ''[[Gossip Girl]]'' (2008–2012), and Father Frank Ignatius in ''[[Evil (American TV series)|Evil]]'' (2022–2024). Shawn is also a playwright; his plays include the [[Obie Award]]–winning ''[[Aunt Dan and Lemon]]'' (1985), ''[[The Designated Mourner]]'' (1996), ''Grasses of a Thousand Colors'' (2008), and ''[[What We Did Before Our Moth Days]]'' (2026). With [[Andre Gregory]], he wrote and starred in the 1981 drama ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]''. He played the title role in ''[[A Master Builder]]'' (2013), a film adaptation of [[Henrik Ibsen]]'s [[The Master Builder|1892 play]].{{cite web|url=http://archrecord.construction.com/news/2014/08/140801-Film-Review-A-Master-Builder.asp|title=Film Review: A Master Builder|last=Ciampaglia|first=Dante A.|date=August 1, 2014|work=[[Architectural Record]]|access-date=November 12, 2014|archive-date=September 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925111838/http://archrecord.construction.com/news/2014/08/140801-Film-Review-A-Master-Builder.asp|url-status=dead}} [[Haymarket Books]] published his books ''Essays'' (2009) and ''Night Thoughts'' (2017). ==Early life and education== Shawn was born in New York City to a [[Jews|Jewish]] family.{{cite magazine|last1=Orel|first1=Gwen|url=http://tabletmag.com/jewish-arts-and-culture/15038/bag-of-tricks|title=Bag of Tricks|magazine=Tablet Magazine|date=September 3, 2009|access-date=March 28, 2015|archive-date=April 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425032154/http://www.tabletmag.com/jewish-arts-and-culture/15038/bag-of-tricks|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last1=Nathan|first1=John|date=7 April 2009|title=Interview: Wallace Shawn. He makes Woody look pretty, but he's a pop culture icon|work=The Jewish Chronicle|url=https://www.thejc.com/life/interview-wallace-shawn-rr3dduu8|access-date=2 November 2020|archive-date=October 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022060614/https://www.thejc.com/culture/interviews/interview-wallace-shawn-1.8709|url-status=live}}{{cite web |author1=((Jewish United Fund)) |author1-link=Jewish United Fund |date=2016 |title=Celebrities: Wallace Shawn |url=https://www.juf.org/celebrities/celebrity.aspx?id=10902 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106101400/https://www.juf.org/celebrities/celebrity.aspx?id=10902 |archive-date=6 November 2019 |website=[[Jewish United Fund]]}}{{cite web|url=http://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board|title=Councils, Staff and Board of Jewish Voice for Peace|work=Jewish Voice for Peace|access-date=December 22, 2017|archive-date=July 24, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724050918/http://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board|url-status=dead}} His parents were journalist Cecille (née Lyon) and [[William Shawn]], the longtime editor of ''[[The New Yorker]]''. He has younger twin siblings: composer [[Allen Shawn]],see pg. 20 of liner notes accompanying "Allen Shawn – Piano Works" CD issued by Coviello Classics label (COV 91414)> {{cite web|url=http://www.covielloclassics.de/index.php/katalog/search/allen%20shawn.html|title=Allen Shawn – Klavierwerke|website=Music Reference|access-date=February 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170204085848/http://www.covielloclassics.de/index.php/katalog/search/allen%20shawn.html|archive-date=February 4, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} and Mary, who is [[autistic]] and lives in an institution.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/30/books/30kaku.html|title=Allen Shawn – Wish I Could Be There: Notes From a Phobic Life – Books – Review|last=Kakutani|first=Michiko|date=January 30, 2007|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date=April 30, 2019|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=October 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022064153/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/30/books/30kaku.html|url-status=live}} William was the son of emigrants from Central Europe.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/12/09/obituaries/william-shawn-85-is-dead-new-yorker-s-gentle-despot.html#:~:text=At%20the%20time%2C%20S.%20I.,than%20a%20destroyer%20of%20it.|last=Pace|first=Eric|date=9 December 1992|title=William Shawn, 85, Is Dead: New Yorker's Gentle Despot|website=The New York Times|access-date=13 January 2025|archive-date=September 3, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250903050811/https://www.nytimes.com/1992/12/09/obituaries/william-shawn-85-is-dead-new-yorker-s-gentle-despot.html#:~:text=At%20the%20time%2C%20S.%20I.,than%20a%20destroyer%20of%20it.|url-status=live}} Shawn grew up on [[Manhattan]]'s [[Upper East Side]].{{cite web| url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2011/02/famous-comedian-dangerous-playwright#:~:text=He%20grew%20up%20on%20Manhattan%27s,have%20collaborated%20on%20an%20opera| title=Profile of actor and playwright Wallace Shawn | Harvard Magazine| date=February 22, 2011| access-date=May 12, 2024| archive-date=August 7, 2024| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240807193616/https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2011/02/famous-comedian-dangerous-playwright#:~:text=He%20grew%20up%20on%20Manhattan%27s,have%20collaborated%20on%20an%20opera| url-status=live}} He attended [[The Collegiate School]] on Manhattan's West Side before transferring to [[The Putney School]], a private liberal arts high school in [[Putney, Vermont]]. After high school, he studied [[history]] at [[Harvard University]], graduating in 1965 with a [[Bachelor of Arts]]. He then studied [[philosophy, politics and economics]], as well as Latin, at [[Magdalen College, Oxford]], originally intending to become a diplomat. He traveled to India as an English teacher on a [[Fulbright]] program.{{Cite news|date=23 December 2021|title=Fulbright Program Celebrates 75 Years of Impact|work=States News Service}} ==Career== {{see also|Wallace Shawn on screen and stage}} ===Playwright=== Shawn's early plays, such as ''[[Marie and Bruce]]'' (1978), portrayed emotional and sexual conflicts in an [[Theatre of the Absurd|absurdist]] style, with language both lyrical and violent. In a conversation with [[Andre Gregory]], parts of which were used to create ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'', Shawn said these plays depicted "my interior life as a raging beast." Critical response was extremely polarized: some critics hailed Shawn as a major writer, while [[John Simon (critic)|John Simon]] called ''Marie and Bruce'' "garbage" and Shawn "one of the unsightliest actors in this city."{{cite news |url=http://theater.nytimes.com/2011/04/06/theater/reviews/in-marie-and-bruce-wallace-shawn-paints-misery-review.html |title=There's Room for Everyone Aboard a Marital Misery Tour |first=Ben |last=Brantley |date=April 5, 2011 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 5, 2017 |archive-date=June 17, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617040959/http://theater.nytimes.com/2011/04/06/theater/reviews/in-marie-and-bruce-wallace-shawn-paints-misery-review.html |url-status=live }} His 1977 play ''A Thought in Three Parts'' caused controversy in London when the production was investigated by a [[vice squad]] and attacked in Parliament after allegations of pornographic content.{{cite web|url=http://www.whistlerinthedark.com/productions/DanandLemon.html |title=Aunt Dan and Lemon |website=Whistler in the Dark |date=2011 |access-date=July 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323133414/http://www.whistlerinthedark.com/productions/DanandLemon.html |archive-date=March 23, 2012 |url-status=usurped}} Shawn received an [[Obie Award]] for playwrighting in 1975, for ''Our Late Night''.1975 Obie Awards https://www.obieawards.com/events/1970s/year-75/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609085045/https://www.obieawards.com/events/1970s/year-75/ |date=June 9, 2023 }} [[File:Wallace Shawn.jpg|left|thumb|302x302px|Shawn in 2005]] Shawn's later plays are more overtly political, drawing parallels between his characters' psychology and the behavior of governments and social classes. Among the best-known of these are ''[[Aunt Dan and Lemon]]'' (1985) and ''[[The Designated Mourner]]'' (1997). Shawn's political work has invited controversy, as he often presents the audience with several contradictory points of view. He has called ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'' a cautionary tale against [[fascism]]. Shawn's monologue ''The Fever'', originally meant to be performed for small audiences in apartments, depicts a person who becomes sick while struggling to find a morally consistent way to live when faced with injustice, and harshly criticizes the United States' record in supporting oppressive [[anti-communist]] regimes. In 1997, Shawn discussed the political nature of ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'', ''The Fever'' and ''The Designated Mourner'' in an interview in which he talked extensively about the thematic connections among them, as well as his own views on [[Marxist]], [[communist]] and [[socialist]] politics, their relevance to [[American liberalism]], and how governmental and individual responsibilities for finding solutions to the dichotomy between rich and poor in the world take hold in his characters.{{cite web|last=McGrath|first=Patrick|date=Spring 1997|title=Wallace Shawn by Patrick McGrath|url=http://bombsite.com/issues/59/articles/2063|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406140744/http://bombmagazine.org/article/2063/|archive-date=April 6, 2016|access-date=July 29, 2014|website=Bomb Magazine}} ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'' earned Shawn his second Obie Award for playwrighting in 1986,Obie Awards [http://www.obieawards.com/events/1980s/year-86/ "1986 Winners"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306082529/http://www.obieawards.com/events/1980s/year-86/ |date=March 6, 2018 }} and ''The Fever'' won an Obie for Best American Play in 1991.Obie Awards, [http://www.obieawards.com/events/1990s/year-91/ "1991 Winners"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721192250/http://www.obieawards.com/events/1990s/year-91/ |date=July 21, 2018 }} Three of Shawn's plays have been adapted into films: ''The Designated Mourner'' (basically a film version of [[David Hare (dramatist)|David Hare]]'s stage production), ''Marie and Bruce'' and ''The Fever''. [[Vanessa Redgrave]] stars in ''[[The Fever (2004 film)|The Fever]]'' (2004),{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/review-television-fever-dc-idUSN1230003820070612 |title=Redgrave laid low by HBO's heavy "Fever" |website=[[Reuters]] |date=June 12, 2007 |first=Ray |last=Richmond |access-date=January 5, 2017 |archive-date=July 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721192054/https://www.reuters.com/article/review-television-fever-dc-idUSN1230003820070612 |url-status=live }} which first aired on [[HBO]] on June 13, 2007.{{Cite news |last=Kahn |first=Robert |date=2007-07-08 |title=Fast Chat: Vanessa Redgrave |work=Newsday |pages=c-3}} Shawn has also written political commentary for ''[[The Nation]]'', and in 2004 he published the one-issue-only progressive political magazine ''Final Edition'', which featured interviews with and articles by [[Jonathan Schell]], [[Noam Chomsky]], [[Mark Strand]] and [[Deborah Eisenberg]]. Shawn is credited as translator of [[Bertolt Brecht]]'s ''[[The Threepenny Opera]]'', which opened at [[Studio 54]] in [[Manhattan]] on March 25, 2006. He appeared briefly in voiceover during "Song about the Futility of Human Endeavor". He published his first nonfiction work, ''Essays'', on September 1, 2009. It is a collection of essays that express his perceptions of politics and other aspects of his life.{{Cite journal |last=Jameson |first=A.D |date=2010 |title=Wallace Shawn. Essays. |journal=The Review of Contemporary Fiction |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=167+ |via=Gale Literature}} ===Acting=== Shawn's involvement with theater began in 1970 when he met [[Andre Gregory]], who has since directed several of his plays. As a stage actor, he has appeared mostly in his own plays and other projects with Gregory. He made his film debut in 1979, playing [[Diane Keaton]]'s ex-husband in [[Woody Allen]]'s ''[[Manhattan (1979 film)|Manhattan]]'' and an insurance agent in [[Bob Fosse]]'s ''[[All That Jazz (film)|All That Jazz]]''. His best-known film roles include Earl in ''[[Strange Invaders]]'' (1983) and Mr. Hall in ''[[Clueless]]'' (1995). After seeing his performance in ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'' (1981), casting director Janet Hirshenson was so fond of his delivery of the word "inconceivable" that she cast him as Vizzini in ''[[The Princess Bride]]'' (1987), for whom the word is a catchphrase. Other roles include Baron Von Westphalen in ''[[Southland Tales]]'', Cyrus Rose on ''[[Gossip Girl]]'', Marty in ''[[Vegas Vacation]]'' (1997), and Ezra in ''[[The Haunted Mansion (2003 film)|The Haunted Mansion]]'' (2003).{{Cite news|last=Morris|first=Wesley|date=2007-11-16|title=Out on the edge, scavenging among 'Southland Tales|work=Boston Globe}}{{Cite news|last=Itzkoff|first=Dave|date=2008-11-17|title=Wallace Shawn on 'Gossip Girl'? It's Not Inconceivable: The Arts/Cultural Desk |work=New York Times}}{{Cite news|last=Chaney|first=Jen|date=2003-11-28|title='The Haunted Mansion' A Familiar Fun House|newspaper=Washington Post}} [[File:Wallace Shawn 2014 (cropped).jpg|thumb|288x288px|Shawn in 2014]] His rare non-comedic film roles include two collaborations with [[Andre Gregory]] and [[Louis Malle]]: the semi-autobiographical dialogue ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'', and a combined production-and-backstage-drama of ''[[Uncle Vanya]]'' titled ''[[Vanya on 42nd Street]]''. Shawn quite often appears on television, where he has appeared in many genres and series. He has had recurring roles as the [[Grand Nagus Zek]] on ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', Stuart Best on ''[[Murphy Brown]]'', Jeff Engels on ''[[The Cosby Show]]'', Dr. Howard Stiles on ''[[Crossing Jordan]]'', Arnie Ross on ''[[Taxi (TV series)|Taxi]]'', Charles Lester on both ''[[The Good Wife]]'' and ''[[The Good Fight]]'', a reprisal of his role as Mr. Hall on ''[[Clueless (TV series)|Clueless]]'' (based on the film), and Father Frank Ignatius on ''[[Evil (American TV series)|Evil]]''. He appeared in the 1985 music video for [[Chaka Khan]]'s "This Is My Night". On February 4, 2010, Shawn appeared as Alan Rubin on ''[[The Daily Show with Jon Stewart]]''. ''[[A Master Builder]]'' opened in New York City in June 2014. In 2018, he joined the cast of ''[[Young Sheldon]]'' in the recurring role of Meemaw's boyfriend and Sheldon's physics professor, Dr. John Sturgis.{{cite web|title=Wallace Shawn returns as Dr. Sturgis on Young Sheldon|work=Monsters and Critics|url=https://www.monstersandcritics.com/smallscreen/wallace-shawn-returns-as-dr-sturgis-on-young-sheldon/|access-date=27 February 2019|date=October 18, 2018|archive-date=February 28, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190228065922/https://www.monstersandcritics.com/smallscreen/wallace-shawn-returns-as-dr-sturgis-on-young-sheldon/|url-status=live}} Shawn starred in Woody Allen's 2020 film ''[[Rifkin's Festival]]'', set in [[San Sebastián]], Spain.{{cite news |title=Woody Allen to Begin Filming New Movie This Summer |first=Nate |last=Nickolai |work=Variety |date=June 4, 2019 |url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/woody-allen-christoph-waltz-gina-gershon-spain-1203232841/ |archive-date=November 2, 2019 |access-date=June 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102160813/https://variety.com/2019/film/news/woody-allen-christoph-waltz-gina-gershon-spain-1203232841/ |url-status=live }} Shawn was honored in 2005 with the [[PEN/Laura Pels International Foundation for Theater Award]] as a Master American Dramatist.{{Cite news |date=May 10, 2005|last=Hernandez|first=Ernio |url=https://playbill.com/article/wallace-shawn-and-dael-orlandersmith-win-2005-pen-laura-pels-awards-for-drama-com-125784|title= Wallace Shawn and Dael Orlandersmith Win 2005 PEN/Laura Pels Awards for Drama|website=Playbill|access-date=March 5, 2026}} ====Voice acting==== Shawn is a voice actor for animated films and television series, including the ''[[Toy Story (franchise)|Toy Story]]'' franchise, ''[[Monsters, Inc.]]'' (during the outtakes in the closing credits), ''[[Kingdom Hearts III]]'', ''[[The Incredibles]]'', ''[[A Goofy Movie]]'', ''[[Family Guy]]'', ''[[Happily N'Ever After]]'', ''[[Tom and Jerry: Shiver Me Whiskers]]'', ''[[Regular Show]]'', ''[[BoJack Horseman]]'' and ''[[Animal Crackers (2017 film)|Animal Crackers]]''. Shawn said that ''Toy Story'' director [[John Lasseter]] might have seen both ''My Dinner with Andre'' and ''The Princess Bride'' and seen him as "excitable" like Shawn's character, Rex.{{cite web |url=https://triblive.com/aande/more-a-and-e/wallace-shawn-talks-acting-princess-bride-and-toy-story/ |first=Steve |last=Segal |date=December 4, 2019 |work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |title=''Wallace Shawn talks acting, 'Princess Bride' and 'Toy Story' ahead of Steel City Con'' |access-date=December 4, 2019 |archive-date=August 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240830235927/https://triblive.com/aande/more-a-and-e/wallace-shawn-talks-acting-princess-bride-and-toy-story/ |url-status=live }} During production of ''[[The Fox and the Hound]]'', Shawn was originally cast as Boomer, but dropped out and was replaced by [[Paul Winchell]].{{Cite news |date=June 19, 2015 |title=We Bet You Didn't Know These Actors Voice Characters in Both Disney and Disney Pixar Movies |url=https://ohmy.disney.com/movies/2015/06/18/we-bet-you-didnt-know-these-actors-voice-characters-in-both-disney-and-disneypixar-movies/ |url-status=dead |access-date=September 14, 2017 |work=Oh My Disney|last1=Taylor|first1=Drew|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915024415/https://ohmy.disney.com/movies/2015/06/18/we-bet-you-didnt-know-these-actors-voice-characters-in-both-disney-and-disneypixar-movies/ |archive-date=September 15, 2017 }} In ''[[Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore]]'', he replaced [[Jon Lovitz]] as the voice of [[List of Cats & Dogs characters#Calico|Calico]]. He also voiced Mr. Mustela in ''[[The Addams Family 2]]''.{{Cite web |url=https://www.kcci.com/article/the-addams-family-2/37827917 |last=Fudge |first=Damond |title=Movie Review: 'The Addams Family 2' |website=[[KCCI]] |date=October 1, 2021 |access-date=March 5, 2026 |archive-date=January 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119235902/https://www.kcci.com/article/the-addams-family-2/37827917 |url-status=live }} ==Political activity== Shawn has written many plays with [[socialist]] themes; much of his work examines the "connective tissue between private psychology and the politics of inequality".{{Cite web |last=Hughley |first=Marty |title=DramaWatch: Wallace Shawn in a 'Fever' • Oregon ArtsWatch |url=https://www.orartswatch.org/dramawatch-wallace-shawn-in-a-fever/ |access-date=2024-11-18 |language=en-US |archive-date=November 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127202057/https://www.orartswatch.org/dramawatch-wallace-shawn-in-a-fever/ |url-status=live }} He identifies as a socialist in the 2011 essay "Why I Call Myself a Socialist: Is the World Really a Stage?", which was published online and later in his ''Essays''.{{cite news |last=Shawn |first=Wallace |date=February 3, 2011 |title=Why I Call Myself a Socialist: Is the World Really a Stage? |website=[[Huffington Post]] |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/wallace-shawn/why-i-call-myself-a-socia_b_818061.html |access-date=January 5, 2017 |archive-date=March 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313021836/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/wallace-shawn/why-i-call-myself-a-socia_b_818061.html |url-status=live }} In June 2013, Shawn and many other public figures appeared in a video showing support for [[Chelsea Manning]], a U.S. Army soldier imprisoned for leaking classified material.{{cite web |last=Gavin |first=Patrick |date=June 20, 2013 |title=Celeb video: 'I am Bradley Manning' |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2013/06/celebrity-bradley-manning-video-93041.html#ixzz2WgfpNmys |access-date=July 29, Wallace Shawn, Deborah Eisenberg, Fran Lebowitz (6160564537).jpg|left|thumb|270x270px|Shawn (center, left) at the [[Brooklyn Book Festival]] in 2014]] Shawn voiced his support for the [[Palestinian people]] during the [[2014 Gaza War]].{{Cite news |last=Shawn |first=Wallace |date=August 25, 2014 |title=Wallace Shawn on Gaza: "The Anger of the Palestinians Cannot Be Ended by Killing Their Children" |language=en |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |location=Los Angeles, California |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/wallace-shawn-gaza-anger-palestinians-727193 |access-date=December has been on the advisory board of [[Jewish Voice for Peace]].{{cite web |author= |date= |title=Advisory Board |url=https://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board | website=jewishvoiceforpeace.org |publisher=Jewish Voice for Peace |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721071612/https://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board |archive-date=21 July 2015 |access-date=3 March 2025}} On October 16, 2023, Shawn spoke at a Washington, D.C., rally organized by Jewish Voice for Peace and [[IfNotNow]].{{Cite magazine |last=White |first=Abbey {{nihongo|'''Hideo Ishikawa'''|石川 英郎|Ishikawa Hideo|born December 13, 1969}} is a Japanese [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]] and [[narrator]] from [[Hyōgo Prefecture]], Japan. He is currently affiliated with [[Aoni Production]]. He is known for being the voice of Kicchō Fukuda in ''[[Slam Dunk (manga)|Slam Dunk]]'', [[Jūshirō Ukitake]] in ''[[Bleach (TV series)|Bleach]]'', [[Auron (Final Fantasy)|Auron]] in ''[[Final Fantasy X]]'', [[Itachi Uchiha]] in ''[[Naruto]]'', [[Squall Leonhart]] in the ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' and ''[[Kingdom Hearts]]'' series, Pierre de Chaltier in ''[[Tales of Destiny]]'', and Ryoma Nagare in ''[[Getter Robo]]'' and ''[[Super Robot Wars]]''.

{{Short description|Japanese voice actor (born 1980)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2017}} {{Infobox person | name = Tomokazu Sugita | image = Tomokazu_Sugita_Profile_JGEPA.jpg | alt = | caption = | native_name = 杉田 智和 | native_name_lang = ja | birth_name = | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1980|10|11}} | birth_place = [[Ranzan, Saitama]],{{cite web|script-title=ja:朝日新聞デジタル：（かぞくの肖像）杉田智和さんと直司|url=http://www.asahi.com/special/news/articles/TKY201305230198.html|work=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|access-date=2020-03-05|language=ja}} Japan | occupation = {{flatlist| * [[Voice acting in Japan|Voice actor]] * author }} | years_active = 1998–present | other_names = {{nihongo|Sugi|杉}}{{cite book|year=2007|author=アニメディア編集部・編|script-title=ja:ボイスクロニクル 声の年代記|publisher=[[Gakken]]|page=43|isbn=978-4-05-604923-7}}
{{nihongo|Tomo|トモちゃん|Tomo-chan}}{{cite tweet|number=250614276975370240|user=Mari_navi|title=@sugitaLOV 動揺するトモちゃんペロペロ（笑）|date=September 25, 2012}}{{cite tweet|number=255291325795139586|user=Mari_navi|title=@sugitaLOV やややややめろよトモちゃん！恥ずかしいだろう！！！|date=October 8, 2012}} | agent = {{plainlist| *Myuras (1998–2001) *Atomic Monkey (2001–2020) *AGRS (2020–present){{cite web|script-title=ja:杉田智和 新会社設立 及び 同社へ所属移管のお知らせ|url=http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/archives/3727|access-date=2020-04-01|date=April 2020 }} }} | website = {{URL|https://agrs.co.jp/}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Tomokazu Sugita'''|杉田 智和|Sugita Tomokazu|born October 11, 1980}} is a Japanese [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]] and [[author]].{{Cite web|script-title=ja:株式会社AGRS|url=https://agrs.co.jp/|website=株式会社AGRS|language=ja|access-date=2020-05-04}} He mainly plays young men and is characterized by his "deep bass voice,"{{cite book|year=2013|title=Nikkei Entertainment Anime Special Voice Actor Bible|page=107|publisher=[[Nikkei Business Publications]]|isbn=978-4-8222-7576-1}} and he often performs ad-libs and imitations.{{cite web|url=https://tower.jp/artist/321514/%E6%9D%89%E7%94%B0%E6%99%BA%E5%92%8C|script-title=ja:杉田智和詳細|work=Tower Records|access-date=2017-12-10}} He is best known for his roles as [[Gintoki Sakata]] in ''[[Gintama]]'' and [[Joseph Joestar]] in ''[[JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (TV series)|JoJo's Bizarre Adventure]].'' {{TOC limit}} ==Career== Sugita was born in [[Ranzan, Saitama]]. When he was in elementary school and watched the TV anime ''[[Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai]]'', he noticed that the character Hyunckel had a much lower voice than he had imagined from reading the original manga, and thought he was "still cool," but the moment he said his special move, Sugita realized that it was the same voice as Phoenix Ikki from ''[[Saint Seiya]]'' ([[Hideyuki Hori]]).{{Cite book|year=2014|title=Nikkei Entertainment! Anime Special Voice Actor Bible 2015|publisher=[[Nikkei Business Publications]]|page=48|isbn=978-4-8222-7595-2}} In junior high school, he was a member of the tennis club and served as the head of the club, while in high school, he joined the [[Shorinji Kempo]] club (1-dan).{{Cite web|url=http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/amprofile/sugita.html|script-title=ja:杉田 智和=|publisher=Atomic Monkey|access-date=2013-05-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218084240/http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/amprofile/sugita.html|archive-date=2013-02-18|url-status=dead}} When he was a child, he wanted to be a temple priest, and in high school he wanted to be a home economics teacher, a confectioner, or a designer. At the time, when he thought about writing a script for a stage performance at a school event and added sound effects and background music to a recording of his own voice, his older brother heard it and suggested that he try to find a job that made use of his voice and speech, which led him to become a voice actor. While still in high school, he won the Myuras & [[Animage]] Award at the Voice Actor Spring School sponsored by the Japan Narration Actor Institute, and entered the Myuras Actors School (now the Vocal and Dance Division of the Japan Narration Actor Institute), while at the same time belonging to the Myuras entertainment agency.{{Cite web|url=https://anime.eiga.com/person/11078/|script-title=ja:杉田智和：声優情報 – アニメハック|access-date=2019-07-23}} At the age of 17, he made his voice acting debut as a gift announcement narrator for ''[[Kamen Rider (1971 TV series)|Kamen Rider]]'' on [[SKY PerfecTV!]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/plus/anime/entry/2019/018883.html|script-title=ja:「銀魂」銀さん役の杉田智和が登場！"面白くない"過去話を告白：声優ケンユウ倶楽部|publisher=テレ東プラス|date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-07-23}} In 1999, when he was a prep school student, he got his first regular role in an anime production with ''[[Cybuster]]'', and continued his voice acting career while studying until he graduated from university. After the dissolution of Myuras in 2001, he joined Atomic Monkey after a period of freelancing, and made his first leading role playing [[List of Chobits characters|Hideki Motosuwa]] in the anime series ''[[Chobits]]''. Sugita played the leading roles in both ''[[Gintama]]'' ([[Gintoki Sakata]]) and ''[[Haruhi Suzumiya|The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya]]'' ([[Kyon]]), greatly increasing his fame. In 2009, he won the Best Actor in supporting role award at the [[3rd Seiyu Awards]].{{cite news|title=3rd Annual Seiyū Award Winners Officially Announced (Updated)|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-07/3rd-annual-seiyu-award-winners-officially-announced|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=March 7, 2009|access-date=March 4, 2014}} In October 2013, he won the Male Voice Actor Award at the "[[Newtype]] x Machi★Asobi Anime Awards 2013", and his role in ''[[Gargantia on the Verdurous Planet]]'', Chamber K6821, also won the Mascot Character Award.{{cite web|url=https://webnewtype.com/special/animeaward/2013/|title=Newtype Anime Awards 2013|publisher=WebNewtype|access-date=2019-07-23|archive-date=July 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723123758/https://webnewtype.com/special/animeaward/2013/|url-status=dead}} In 2010, he starred in a live-action film ''[[Wonderful World (2010 film)|Wonderful World]]'', alongside [[Mamoru Miyano]], [[Tomokazu Seki]], [[Rikiya Koyama]], [[Yuka Hirata]], [[Showtaro Morikubo]] and [[Daisuke Namikawa]].""{{cite news|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-12-08/namikawa-directs-1st-film/live-action-wonderful-world|title=Namikawa Directs 1st Film: Live-Action ''Wonderful World''|date=December 8, 2009|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=January 30, 2010}} On April 1, 2020, Sugita left Atomic Monkey, the company he had been affiliated with for many years, and established AGRS Inc. with Kai Itō, a lawyer well versed in the entertainment industry, as an advisor and himself as the representative director. ==Personal life== Sugita's [[mongrel]] dog, "Naoji" ({{lang|ja|直司}}), was adopted by his father from the original owner. He has once taken a commercial for [[4gamer]] with his dog.{{cite web |script-title=ja:【杉田智和】4GamerのCM【マフィア梶田】 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDIanP0jEMI |via=YouTube | date=May 7, 2013 |language=en}} Naoji died on 6 September 2018.{{cite web |script-title=ja:実家から直司が亡くなったとの連絡を受けました。享年17歳。彼ほど世界中に愛された雑種犬はいないと思います。ありがとうございました。|url=https://twitter.com/sugitaLOV/status/1037556719969128449 |via=Twitter |language=ja}} His favorite colors are black and silver. {{Nihongo|'''Hiroki Takahashi'''|高橋 広樹|Takahashi Hiroki}} is a Japanese actor, [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]], and singer. His major roles include [[List of The Prince of Tennis characters#Eiji Kikumaru|Eiji Kikumaru]] in ''[[The Prince of Tennis]]'', Tobias in ''[[Pokémon (TV series)|Pokémon]]'', [[List of School Rumble characters#Kenji Harima|Kenji Harima]] in ''[[School Rumble]]'', [[List of Hunter × Hunter characters#Hisoka Morow|Hisoka]] in ''[[Hunter × Hunter|Hunter × Hunter (1999)]]'', [[Katsuya Jonouchi]] in ''[[Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters]]'', and Takato Saijō in ''[[Dakaichi]]''. On video games, he voiced [[Ryu (Street Fighter)|Ryu]] in the ''[[Street Fighter]]'' series.

== Personal life ==
Takahashi is married to voice actress Aiko Aihashi. Their first son was born on June 24, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2016-06-24/voice-actors-hiroki-takahashi-aiko-aihashi-welcome-baby-boy/.103550|title=Voice Actors Hiroki Takahashi, Aiko Aihashi Welcome Baby Boy|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2019}}</ref>

{{short description|Japanese-American actress (born 1966)}} {{Use American English|date=December 2022}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2022}} {{family name hatnote|[[Tomita]]|lang=Japanese}} {{Infobox person | name = Tamlyn Tomita | image = Andres Useche and Tamlyn Tomita (cropped).jpg | caption = Tomita in 2010 | birth_name = Tamlyn Naomi Tomita | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1966|1|27}} | birth_place = [[Okinawa (city)|Okinawa City]], [[United States Civil Administration of the Ryukyu Islands|Ryukyu Islands]] (now [[Japan]]) | education = [[University of California, Los Angeles]] | occupation = Actress | years_active = 1986–present | spouse = Daniel Blinkoff
({{abbr|m.|married}} 2021) }} '''Tamlyn Naomi Tomita''' (born January 27, 1966){{cite web |title=Tamlyn Tomita |url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/192816%7C0/Tamlyn-Tomita/#overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524050326/http://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/192816%7C0/Tamlyn-Tomita/#overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 24, 2018 |website=[[Turner Classic Movies]] |access-date=August 27, 2022}} is a Japanese-American actress. She made her screen debut as [[Kumiko (character)|Kumiko]] in ''[[The Karate Kid Part II]]'' (1986) and reprised the character for the streaming series ''[[Cobra Kai]]'' (2021). She is also well known for her role as [[The Joy Luck Club (novel)#Waverly Jong|Waverly]] in ''[[The Joy Luck Club (film)|The Joy Luck Club]]'' (1993). Additional films include ''[[Come See the Paradise]]'' (1990), ''[[Picture Bride (film)|Picture Bride]]'' (1994), ''[[Four Rooms]]'' (1995), ''[[Robot Stories]]'' (2003), ''[[The Day After Tomorrow]]'' (2004) and ''[[Gaijin 2: Love Me as I Am]]'' (2005). Tomita also has played several recurring roles on television series, including ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]'', ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', ''[[Teen Wolf (2011 TV series)|Teen Wolf]], [[Eureka (2006 TV series)|Eureka]],'' and ''[[How to Get Away with Murder]]''. She starred on the [[Epix]] drama series ''[[Berlin Station (TV series)|Berlin Station]]'' (2016), and in 2017 began starring in the ABC medical drama ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]''. In 2020, she had a recurring role in ''[[Star Trek: Picard]]''. She also released a solo album "Sweet Surprise" exclusively in Japan. ==Early life and education== Tamlyn Tomita, a second generation Japanese-American ([[nisei]]), was born January 27, 1966,{{cite web|title=Celebrity birthdays for the week of Jan. 22-28|website=The Associated Press|date=January 17, 2023|accessdate=January 27, 2023|url=https://apnews.com/article/entertainment-country-music-tv-celebrity-birthdays-teddy-gentry-07ff63620f848616f7521abdbd6706da}} on a U.S. military base in [[Okinawa (city)|Okinawa]] and grew up in [[Los Angeles]].{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/1991/01/25/close-tamlyn-tomita/ |title=Close-up on Tamlyn Tomita -- We talk to the actress from ''Come See the Paradise'' |access-date=January 6, 2021 |last=Adato |first=Alison |date=January 25, 1991 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly }}{{cite web |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=qGiRtLT0P00 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/qGiRtLT0P00| archive-date=December 12, 2021|url-status=live|title=Tamlyn Tomita Reveals Her Parents' Love Story |work=Kababayan Weekly|via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=May 10, 2020}}{{cbignore}} Her Japanese-American father was in an [[Internment of Japanese Americans|internment camp]] during [[World War II]]. He met her mother while stationed in [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] between the [[Korean War|Korean]] and [[Vietnam War]]s. Her mother was of half-[[Ryukyuan people|Native Okinawan]] and half-[[Filipinos|Filipino]] descent, born in [[Manila]] and emigrated to Okinawa after [[World War II]]. Her father became a [[LAPD]] officer upon returning to Los Angeles. Tomita graduated from [[Granada Hills High School]]{{cite magazine |url=https://news.yahoo.com/reprise-her-karate-kid-role-204635077.html |title='Good Doctor' Star Tamlyn Tomita Says "Stop Treating Me As A Woman: Treat Me As An Equal" |access-date=January 7, 2021 |last=Block |first=Jenny |date=April 23, 2018 |magazine=swaay.com }} and attended [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where she studied history and planned to become a history teacher.{{cite magazine |url=https://news.yahoo.com/reprise-her-karate-kid-role-204635077.html |title=To reprise her 'Karate Kid' role in 'Cobra Kai,' Tamlyn Tomita had some ground rules |access-date=January 4, 2021 |last=Yamato |first=Jen |date=January 1, 2021 |magazine=Los Angeles Times }} While a junior at UCLA, she participated in [[Nisei Week]], where she was crowned its 1984 queen.{{cite magazine |url=https://niseiweek.org/queen-court/#past-courts |title=Past Queens & Courts |access-date=January 7, 2021 |magazine=[[Nisei Week]] }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} She and several other Japanese-American girls were asked by Helen Funai, the 1963 pageant queen, to audition for the role of Kumiko in ''[[The Karate Kid II]]''.{{cite magazine |url=https://caamedia.org/blog/2017/10/30/talking-with-tamlyn-tomita-the-actress-dishes-on-independent-cinema-and-whitewashing/ |title=Talking with Tamkyn Tomita: The Actress Dishes on Independent Cinema and Whitewashing |access-date=January 7, 2021 |date=October 30, 2017 |magazine=[[Center for Asian American Media]] }} She promised her parents that she would finish college, and then explore acting. ==Career== ===Film=== After ''[[The Karate Kid Part II]]'' (1986), Tomita had major roles in a number of [[independent movie]]s. Her biggest role was in the 1990 drama film ''[[Come See the Paradise]]''.{{cite web|url=https://ew.com/article/1991/01/25/close-tamlyn-tomita/|title=Tamlyn Tomita|work=EW.com|access-date=27 December 2014|archive-date=December 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227222024/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,313112,00.html|url-status=live}} In 1993, she co-starred opposite [[Ming-Na Wen]] in the [[ensemble cast]] drama ''[[The Joy Luck Club (film)|The Joy Luck Club]]'' and the next year she had a role in the 1994 independent film ''[[Picture Bride (film)|Picture Bride]]''. In 1995 Tomita appeared alongside [[Antonio Banderas]] in the [[Robert Rodriguez]]-directed segment of the [[Vignette (literature)|vignette]] [[anthology]] comedy ''[[Four Rooms]]''.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/12/26/movies/film-review-hellish-guests-in-kinky-spats-in-four-rooms.html|title=FILM REVIEW;Hellish Guests in Kinky Spats in 'Four Rooms'|newspaper=The New York Times |date=26 December 1995|access-date=27 December 2014|last1=Maslin |first1=Janet }} In the 21st century, Tomita has had roles in other independent films and co-starred in several major Hollywood productions, including playing Janet Tokada in ''[[The Day After Tomorrow]]''. In 2005, she starred in the Brazilian drama film ''[[Gaijin 2: Love Me as I Am]]'' and also had a leading role in the independent film ''[[Robot Stories]]'' in 2003. She was also in ''[[Only the Brave (2006 film)|Only the Brave]]'' about the [[Japanese American]] segregated fighting unit, the [[442nd Regimental Combat Team]] of World War II, which included two other ''Karate Kid'' stars, [[Yuji Okumoto]] and [[Pat Morita]].{{cite web |url=http://konakitchen.com/meet-yuji/ |title=Meet Yuji Okumoto |access-date=2021-01-06 |publisher=konakitchen.com }} ===Television=== Tomita appeared as a character named Ming Li on the [[NBC]] daytime soap opera ''[[Santa Barbara (TV series)|Santa Barbara]]'' from May to September 1988.{{cite web|url=http://santabarbara-online.com/mingli2.htm|title=Ming Li|website=santabarbara-online.com|access-date=24 October 2017}} In 1994, she guest-starred in the first episode of season 3 of ''[[Highlander: The Series]]''. In 2008, she made her return to daytime soaps with a recurring role on ABC's ''[[General Hospital]]''.{{cite news|url=http://daytimeconfidential.com/2008/04/25/general-hospital-tamlyn-tomita-cast-as-kate-howard-rival/|title=General Hospital: Tamlyn Tomita Cast As Kate Howard Rival|work=Daytime Confidential|access-date=27 December 2014}} In 2012, she had another recurring role on NBC's ''[[Days of Our Lives]]''. From 1996 to 1997, Tomita was a regular cast member in the short-lived [[UPN]] drama series, ''[[The Burning Zone]]''. In 1993, she appeared in the pilot movie for ''[[Babylon 5]]'' as Lt. Commander Takashima, second-in-command of the titular space station, but she declined the opportunity to continue as a cast member of the subsequent series. During her career she has guest starred on shows such as ''[[Seven Days (TV series)|Seven Days]]''; ''[[Quantum Leap (1989 TV series)|Quantum Leap]]''; ''[[Living Single]]''; ''[[Murder, She Wrote]]''; ''[[Chicago Hope]]''; ''[[Will & Grace]]''; ''[[Nash Bridges]]''; ''[[The Shield]]''; ''[[Strong Medicine]]''; ''[[Stargate SG-1]]''; ''[[Stargate: Atlantis]]''; ''[[The Mentalist]]''; ''[[Private Practice (TV series)|Private Practice]]''; ''[[True Blood]]''; ''[[Zoo (American TV series)|Zoo]]''; ''[[Tour of Duty (TV series)|Tour of Duty]]''; ''[[Criminal Minds]]''; and many other dramas and comedies. She had longer term recurring roles on ''[[Crossing Jordan]]'', ''[[JAG (TV series)|JAG]]'', ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]'', ''[[Eureka (2006 TV series)|Eureka]]'', ''[[Heroes (American TV series)|Heroes]]'', ''[[Law & Order: LA|Law & Order: Los Angeles]]'', ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', ''[[Teen Wolf (2011 TV series)|Teen Wolf]]'', ''[[Resurrection (U.S. TV series)|Resurrection]]'', ''[[How to Get Away with Murder]]'', and ''[[Chasing Life]]''. In 2016, Tomita played a series regular role on the [[Epix]] drama series ''[[Berlin Station (TV series)|Berlin Station]]''. From 2017 to 2019 she was a [[recurring character]] on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] medical drama ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]''.{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/09/the-good-doctor-tamlyn-tomita-promoted-series-regular-abc-drama-freddie-highmore-1202174900/|title='The Good Doctor': Tamlyn Tomita Upped To Series Regular On ABC Drama|first=Denise|last=Petski|date=22 September 2017|access-date=24 October 2017}} Tomita began a recurring role as the Vulcan/Romulan hybrid Commodore Oh on the [[CBS All Access]] [[web television]] series ''[[Star Trek: Picard]]'' in 2020. In 2021, she reprised her 1980s role as [[Kumiko (character)|Kumiko]] for two episodes in Season 3 of ''[[Cobra Kai]]'', a television sequel to the ''[[The Karate Kid (franchise)|Karate Kid]]'' films.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.etonline.com/cobra-kai-tamlyn-tomita-on-returning-as-kumiko-more-than-30-years-after-karate-kid-exclusive-158658 |title='Cobra Kai': Tamlyn Tomita on Returning as Kumiko More Than 30 Years After 'Karate Kid' (Exclusive) |access-date=2021-01-07 |last=Ng |first=Phillana |date=2021-01-07 |magazine=Entertainment Tonight }}{{cite magazine |url=https://datebook.sfchronicle.com/movies-tv/tamlyn-tomita-returns-to-karate-kid-world-for-season-three-of-cobra-kai |title='Karate Kid II' kicked off Tamlyn Tomita's career. Now she's back, 34 years later, in 'Cobra Kai.' |access-date=2021-01-04 |last=Meeks |first=Karen |date=2020-12-31 |magazine=San Francisco Chronicle }} == Personal life == Tomita has been married twice. '''Richard Steven Horvitz'''{{efn|Horvitz has occasionally been credited as Rico Bonet, Richard Stults, or Richard Wood.}} (born July 29, 1966)<ref>{{cite web | title=Horvitz, Richard Steven 1966– | website=Encyclopedia.com | date=1966-07-29 | url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/horvitz-richard-steven-1966 | access-date=2025-08-09 | archive-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612202624/https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/horvitz-richard-steven-1966 | url-status=live }}</ref> is an American actor, comedian and voice director. He is best known for his voice work in animation and video games. His voice credits include the original [[Alpha 5 (Power Rangers)|Alpha 5]] on ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers]]'', ''[[Power Rangers Zeo]]'' and ''[[Power Rangers Turbo]]'', Razputin Aquato in ''[[Psychonauts]]'', Kaos in ''[[Skylanders]]'', Billy and his father Harold in ''[[Grim & Evil]]'' and ''[[The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy]]'', Grey Matter in ''[[Ben 10 (2005 TV series)|Ben 10]]'', Rodney in ''[[Squirrel Boy]]'', Daggett in ''[[The Angry Beavers]]'', Zim in ''[[Invader Zim]]'', Orthopox in ''[[Destroy All Humans!]]'', the Zoni in ''[[Ratchet & Clank]]'', Bumble in ''[[Kinectimals]]'', the Space Weaver in ''[[Broken Age]]'', Kanchomé in ''[[Zatch Bell!]]'', and [[List of Hazbin Hotel and Helluva Boss characters#Moxxie|Moxxie]] in ''[[Helluva Boss]]''.

==Early life==
Horvitz was born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. His father Louie, a planning engineer for [[Rocketdyne]] for over 35 years, was [[Jewish American|Jewish]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/louie-horvitz-obituary?pid=183947951 | title=Louie Horvitz Obituary (1921–2017) – Legacy Remembers | website=[[Legacy.com]] | access-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-date=June 15, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615031338/https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/louie-horvitz-obituary?pid=183947951 | url-status=live }}</ref> His maternal grandfather was born in [[Cuba]], and his mother's family is from [[Mérida, Yucatán|Mérida, Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sJzACtUqM3k | title=Voice Actors React to Assumptions (@ProZD, @SarahNatochenny1 , Richard Horvitz) | website=[[YouTube]] | date=July 31, 2024 | at=33:48 | quote="I'm half Latino. [...] My mom's family was from Mérida, Mexico. And my grandfather was from Cuba." | access-date=September 26, 2024 | archive-date=September 25, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925154850/https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=Rbxc89TIKxFF6zdm&v=sJzACtUqM3k&feature=youtu.be | url-status=live }}</ref> His older brother, [[Louis J. Horvitz]], is a television director and producer. As a child, Horvitz was inspired by [[Flip Wilson]], [[Tom Jones (singer)|Tom Jones]], and [[Don Adams]], doing impressions of them.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://lancasteronline.com/features/entertainment/richard-horvitz-voice-of-invader-zim-and-other-characters-speaking-at-zenkaikon/article_06167b64-d340-11e4-a5ff-07696390df59.html | title=Richard Horvitz, voice of Invader Zim and other characters, speaking at Zenkaikon | date=25 March 2015 | access-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612204128/https://lancasteronline.com/features/entertainment/richard-horvitz-voice-of-invader-zim-and-other-characters-speaking-at-zenkaikon/article_06167b64-d340-11e4-a5ff-07696390df59.html | url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
===Acting===
[[File:Richard Horvitz JACON 2009 Orlando Florida.png|thumb|Horvitz with an autographed ''[[Invader Zim]]'' picture in May 2009]]
Horvitz first appeared in a 1976 [[Freshen Up]] gum commercial, which led to other commercial appearances and several [[hand model]]ing jobs. After a brief stint in an off-Broadway production of ''[[Oliver!]]'', he went on to make appearances on television series such as ''[[Kids Incorporated]]'' and ''[[Safe at Home (TV series)|Safe at Home]]'', and films such as ''[[Summer School (1987 film)|Summer School]]'', ''[[How I Got into College]]'', and ''[[Deadly Weapon]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Richard S Horvitz Filmography|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/33340/Richard-S-Horvitz/filmography|access-date=25 November 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219175342/https://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/33340/Richard-S-Horvitz/filmography|department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=2013|archive-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> From 1988 to 1991, he starred as Howie for two seasons in the syndicated television sitcom ''[[The Munsters Today]]''.

===Voice acting===
[[File:Richard Steven Horvitz Photo Op GalaxyCon Richmond 2020.jpg|thumb|Horvitz in 2020]]
Starting in 1993, Horvitz changed the focus of his career to voice acting, starting with the voice of Alpha 5 in the live-action series ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers]]''. From there, he had several other voice roles in such animated series as ''[[The Angry Beavers]]'' (as Daggett), ''[[Invader Zim]]'' (as Zim),<ref>{{cite web|last=Bogos|first=Steven|title=Jack Black Heads Broken Age's Voice Acting Cast|url=http://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/127384-Jack-Black-Heads-Broken-Ages-Voice-Acting-Cast|work=Escapist magazine|access-date=25 November 2013|date=2 September 2013}}</ref> ''[[Kim Possible]]'' (as Aviarius), ''[[Dave the Barbarian]]'' (as Ned Frischman), ''[[Zatch Bell!]]'' (as Kanchomé), ''[[The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy]]'' (as Billy and his father Harold),<ref>{{cite web|last=Hackett|first=Keisha|title=Richard Horvitz to join Rikki Simons at Invader Zim Q&A|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/teenlink/fl-tl-richard-horvitz-20130703,0,3307971.story|work=Teen Link/Florida Sun-Sentinel|access-date=25 November 2013|date=July 3, 2013|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203001308/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/teenlink/fl-tl-richard-horvitz-20130703,0,3307971.story|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''[[Ben 10 (2005 TV series)|Ben 10]]'' (as Grey Matter), ''[[Squirrel Boy]]'' (as Rodney), and ''[[Shorty McShorts' Shorts]]'' (as Dudley). He also co-wrote the ''Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy'' episode "Keeper of the Reaper" alongside his wife Kristen Lazarian.

After his stint as Alpha 5 ended, Horvitz went on to voice a few monsters in other ''[[Power Rangers]]'' series and was also the voice of Alpha 7 in the ''[[Power Rangers Wild Force]]'' episode "Forever Red". He voiced the main characters of Raz in the ''[[Psychonauts]]'' series and Orthopox in the ''[[Destroy All Humans!]]'' series. He has also voiced various [[Non-player character|NPCs]] in ''[[EverQuest II]]'', the Berserker Darklings in ''[[The Darkness (video game)|The Darkness]]'', Bumble in ''[[Kinectimals]]'', and Kaos in ''[[Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williams|first=Katie|title=Double Fine shows off Broken Age's voice-acting lineup|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/2013/09/04/double-fine-shows-off-broken-ages-voice-acting-lineup/|work=[[PC Gamer]]|access-date=25 November 2013|date=4 September 2013|archive-date=August 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140824100033/http://www.pcgamer.com/2013/09/04/double-fine-shows-off-broken-ages-voice-acting-lineup/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Horvitz voiced Green Grapes in the [[Fruit of the Loom]] commercials and has acted on stage, including in [[Jeffrey Hatcher]]'s ''Mrs. Mannerly''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Regan|first=Tatum|title=Mrs. Mannerly (Theater Review)|url=http://www.edgeboston.com/index.php?ch=entertainment&sc=theatre&sc2=reviews&sc3=theatre_reviews&id=139024|work=Edge Boston|access-date=25 November 2013|date=Nov 20, 2012|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203030949/http://www.edgeboston.com/index.php?ch=entertainment&sc=theatre&sc2=reviews&sc3=theatre_reviews&id=139024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Horvitz also voices Moxxie and serves as a voice director in the adult animated web series ''[[Helluva Boss]]''. He also played the roles of Alpha 8 and Alpha 9 in the [[Netflix]] special ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: Once & Always]]'', which celebrated the 30th anniversary of the ''Power Rangers'' franchise.<ref name="Thapa screenrant">{{Cite web |last=Thapa |first=Shaurya |date=April 10, 2023 |title=Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: Once & Always Cast & Character Guide |url=https://screenrant.com/mighty-morphin-power-rangers-once-always-cast-character-guide/ |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=April 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429032453/https://screenrant.com/mighty-morphin-power-rangers-once-always-cast-character-guide/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomez |first=Patrick |title=Original 'Power Rangers' stars reunite for 30th anniversary Netflix special |url=https://ew.com/tv/original-power-rangers-netflix-reunion-special-first-look-exclusive-video-photos/ |date=17 January 2023 |access-date=13 March 2023 |website=EW.com |language=en |archive-date=January 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117150704/https://ew.com/tv/original-power-rangers-netflix-reunion-special-first-look-exclusive-video-photos/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Horvitz speaks fluent [[Spanish language|Spanish]], though he has stated he does not perform Spanish-language voice work.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2024 |title=Voice Actors React to Assumptions (@ProZD, @SarahNatochenny1 , Richard Horvitz) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sJzACtUqM3k& |website=[[YouTube]] |at=34:18 |quote="Even though I can speak Spanish fluently, I don't do it. I just don't read for it."}}</ref>

===Comedy===
In 2001, Horvitz was in the [[sketch comedy]] group The MoHos with [[Fred Willard]], created by Willard's wife Mary Lovell.<ref name="richardhovitz"/> He and Willard would sometimes perform on various talk shows including ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'' and ''[[The Tonight Show with Jay Leno]]''. Horvitz also appeared in an episode of ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' in the short segment "Bear City" and briefly appeared on ''[[Tosh.0]]''.<ref name="richardhovitz">{{Cite web|url=https://www.richardhorvitz.com/blog/my-story|title=My story|date=17 July 2019|access-date=September 13, 2020|archive-date=October 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022015746/https://www.richardhorvitz.com/blog/my-story|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Horvitz married playwright and screenwriter Kristen Lazarian on February 9, 1996. They currently live in [[Los Angeles]] and have three sons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kristenlazarian.com/bio|title=Kristen Lazarian: Playwright/Screenwriter – BIO|access-date=May 15, 2020|archive-date=August 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811025641/http://kristenlazarian.com/bio|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She is best known for her voice performances in [[anime]], which include [[Alphonse Elric]] in the ''[[Fullmetal Alchemist]]'' series, [[List of Gintama characters#Kagura|Kagura]] in ''[[Gintama]]'', and [[Happy (manga character)|Happy]] in ''[[Fairy Tail]]'' and ''[[Edens Zero]]'',[https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2020-09-26/j.c-staff-produces-edens-zero-tv-anime-for-april-2021-debut/.164514 J.C. Staff Produces Edens Zero TV Anime for April 2021 Debut] -[[Anime News Network]] and in video games, such as [[Haruka Sawamura]] in the ''[[Yakuza (franchise)|Yakuza]]'' series, Kiana Kaslana in ''[[Honkai Impact 3rd]]'', and Rise Kujikawa from ''[[Persona 4]]''. Because of her roles for characters such as [[Shana (Shakugan no Shana)|Shana]] in ''[[Shakugan no Shana]]'', [[List of The Familiar of Zero characters#Louise|Louise]] in ''[[The Familiar of Zero]]'', [[Nagi Sanzenin]] in ''[[Hayate the Combat Butler]]'', [[Taiga Aisaka]] in ''[[Toradora!]]'', Aguri Madoka/Cure Ace in ''[[DokiDoki! PreCure]]'', and [[Aria the Scarlet Ammo#Aria Holmes Kanzaki|Aria Holmes Kanzaki]] in ''[[Aria the Scarlet Ammo]]'', some of her fans have nicknamed her the "Queen of [[Tsundere]]."{{cite web|url = http://mainichi.jp/enta/mantan/archive/news/2009/03/07/20090307mog00m200025000c.html | script-title=ja:声優アワード：「ツンデレの女王」釘宮理恵さんが主演女優賞に 神谷浩史さん二冠達成 | trans-title = Seiyu Award: "Tsundere Queen" Rie Kugimiya Gets Starring Actress Award, Hiroshi Kamiya Also Awarded|website=[[Mainichi Shimbun]] | date =March 7, 2009|access-date=November 11, 2009|language=ja | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100203160859/http://mainichi.jp/enta/mantan/archive/news/2009/03/07/20090307mog00m200025000c.html | archive-date=February 3, 2010 | url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url = http://mainichi.jp/enta/mantan/graph/anime/20071210/ |script-title=ja:ツンデレカルタ：「私の気持ちも知らないで...」"女王"釘宮理恵が読み手 緊急発売へ |trans-title= Tsundere Card Game: 'Please Don't Understand My Feelings' "Queen" Rie Kugimiya as the Reader to be Sold Soon|website=[[Mainichi Shimbun]]|date=December 10, 2007|access-date=November 11, 2009 | language = ja | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080112163132/http://mainichi.jp/enta/mantan/graph/anime/20071210/ | archive-date=January 12, 2008 | url-status=dead}} She is currently represented by the talent agency [[I'm Enterprise]]. She was nominated for Best Actress in a Leading Role at the [[1st Seiyu Awards]]{{cite web|url=http://www.seiyuawards.jp/|script-title=ja://声優アワード//Seiyu Awards// - 声優アワードは、その年度に「最も印象に残る」声優や作品を対象に、その業績を称える本格的な「声優を対象とするアワード」として2006年に創設されました。日本音声製作者連盟、KADOKAWA、小学館、小学館集英社プロダクション、文化放送、アーイメージがアニメ業界各社と協力し、声優を表彰するものとしては業界最大の舞台を提供し、声優地位の向上に寄与することを目的としています|work=seiyuawards.jp|access-date=June 12, 2016|language=ja}} and for Best Actress in Supporting Role. She also won Best Actress in a Supporting Role with [[Mitsuki Saiga]] at the [[2nd Seiyu Awards]]. Kugimiya won Best Actress in the [[3rd Seiyu Awards]] for the roles as [[Taiga Aisaka]] in ''[[Toradora!]]'' and her work in ''[[Nabari no Ou]]''.{{cite web|script-title=ja:第三回声優アワード受賞者 {{pipe}} //声優アワード//Seiyu Awards//|url=http://www.seiyuawards.jp/winning/winning_03|website=seiyuawards.jp|access-date=October 9, 2015|language=ja}} ==Career== In 1997, she earned her reputation from the company I'm Enterprise & We Flying Award at the first summer school of voice actors sponsored by Japan Narration Institute. Later, she became a member of I'm Enterprise. In 1998, she debuted as a voice actress in the video game ''etude prologue -Shaking heart-'' as Tadami Saeki. From the beginning of her debut, she plays the role of a teenage girl mainly from her childhood, using her voice quality. Later, she was appointed as a juvenile character, such as [[List of Twelve Kingdoms characters#Kingdom of Tai inhabitants|Taiki]] in ''[[Twelve Kingdoms]]'' and [[Alphonse Elric]] in ''[[Fullmetal Alchemist]]'' series. She took charge of various characters. Kugimiya has also voiced several tsundere heroines, including [[List of The Familiar of Zero characters#Louise|Louise]] in ''[[The Familiar of Zero]]'' series, and [[List of Hayate the Combat Butler characters#Nagi Sanzenin|Nagi Sanzenin]] in ''[[Hayate the Combat Butler]]''. In 2008, she won for the Best Actresses in supporting roles at the [[2nd Seiyu Awards]].{{cite web |script-title=ja:第二回声優アワード受賞者 {{!}} //声優アワード//Seiyu Awards// |url=http://www.seiyuawards.jp/winning/winning_02/ |website=www.seiyuawards.jp |access-date=26 September 2019 |language=ja |date=2008}} She won for the Best Actress in leading role at the [[3rd Seiyu Awards]].{{cite web |script-title=ja:第三回声優アワード受賞者 {{!}} //声優アワード//Seiyu Awards// |url=http://www.seiyuawards.jp/winning/winning_03/ |website=www.seiyuawards.jp |access-date=26 September 2019 |language=ja |date=2009}} Within the [[Tamagotchi]] [[fandom]] she is known for her role in the Tamagotchi movies and [[anime]] as Mametchi. {{Short description|American actress and singer (1916–1997)}} {{pp-pc1}} {{Infobox person | name = Adriana Caselotti | image = Adriana Caselotti (1944 RKO Pictures publicity photo).jpg | caption = Caselotti in 1944 | birth_name = Adriana Elena Loretta Caselotti | birth_date = {{birth date|1916|05|06|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]], U.S. | death_date = {{death date and age|1997|01|19|1916|05|06|mf=y}} | death_place = [[Los Angeles]], California, U.S. | occupation = {{Hlist|Actress|voice actress|singer}} | years_active = 1932–1997 | notable_works = Original voice of [[Snow White (Disney character)|Snow White]] in [[Walt Disney]]'s ''[[Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film)|Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs]]'' (1937) | spouse = {{plainlist| * {{marriage|Robert James Chard|1945|reason=divorced}} * {{marriage|Norval Weir Mitchell|1952|1972|reason=his death}} * {{marriage|Joseph Dana Costigan|1972|1982|reason=his death}} * {{marriage|Florian St. Pierre|1989|reason=divorced}} }} | parents = [[Maria Orefice]] (mother)
[[Guido Caselotti]] (father) | relatives = [[Louise Caselotti]] (sister) | awards = [[Disney Legends|Disney Legend]] (1994) }} '''Adriana Elena Loretta Caselotti''' (May 6, 1916 – January 19, 1997) was an American actress and singer. Caselotti was best known as the voice of the [[Snow White (Disney character)|title character]] of the first [[List of Disney theatrical animated features|Walt Disney animated feature]], ''[[Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film)|Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs]]'' (1937), for which she was named a [[Disney Legends|Disney Legend]] in 1994, making her the first female voice-over artist to achieve this. ==Early life== Adriana Elena Loretta Caselotti was born in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]] on May 6, 1916 to an [[Italian Americans|Italian-American]] family.{{Cite web | url=https://comics.ha.com/itm/memorabilia/disney/adriana-caselotti-birth-certificate-passport-and-bank-book-1926-52-total-3-items-/a/7173-97030.s| title=Adriana Caselotti Birth Certificate, Passport, and Bank {{!}} Lot #97030 {{!}} Heritage Auctions| accessdate=18 April 2018| website=Heritage Auctions| language=en}} Her father, [[Guido Caselotti|Guido Luigi Emanuele Caselotti]], was an immigrant from [[Udine]], and worked as a music teacher and vocal coach, and served as the organist for the [[Holy Rosary Church (Bridgeport, Connecticut)|Holy Rosary Church]]; and her mother, [[Maria Orefice|Maria Josephine]] ({{nee|Orefice}}) from [[Casavatore]], was a singer (coloratura soprano) in the [[Teatro dell'Opera di Roma|Royal Opera Theatre of Rome]]. Her older sister, [[Louise Caselotti|Louise]], sang opera and gave voice lessons—[[Maria Callas]] being a student of hers. When Caselotti was seven years old, her family left [[Connecticut]] for Italy, while her mother toured with an opera company. Caselotti was educated and [[Room and board|board]]ed at the San Getulio [[convent]], near [[Rome]]. When her family returned to New York three years later, Caselotti re-learned [[English language|English]] and studied singing with her father.[https://www.nytimes.com/1997/01/21/arts/adriana-caselotti-80-voice-of-snow-white.html "Adriana Caselotti, 80, Voice of ''Snow White''"]; ''New York Times''; Obituary article; 01/21/1997; retrieved October 8, 2017 In 1934, Caselotti attended [[Hollywood High School]] where she sang in the senior class Girls' Glee Club and had a leading role in the school's annual musical, ''[[The Belle of New York (musical)|The Belle of New York]]''.{{cite book | title=Poinsettia Yearbook |date=1934 |publisher=Hollywood High School |location=Hollywood |pages=79, 81 |edition=29}} ==Career== In 1935, after her brief stint as a chorus girl and session singer at [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]], [[Walt Disney]] hired Caselotti as the voice of the heroine, [[Snow White (Disney character)|Snow White]].{{cite web | title=Adriana Caselotti| url=https://d23.com/walt-disney-legend/Adriana-Caselotti| url-status=live|access-date=January 26, 2017| website=D23| publisher=Disney| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908004712/https://d23.com/walt-disney-legend/adriana-caselotti/ |archive-date=2015-09-08 }} She was paid a total of $970 for working on the film ({{Inflation|US|970|1937|fmt=eq}}). She was not credited for the role, and had trouble finding new opportunities later in life. [[Jack Benny]] specifically mentioned that he had asked Walt Disney for permission to use her on his radio show and was told, "I'm sorry, but that voice can't be used anywhere. I don't want to spoil the illusion of Snow White."{{cite news | last=Thomas| first=Bob| title=Singer Still Hopes to Cash in as Voice of Snow White| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=gZVGAAAAIBAJ&sjid=FvgMAAAAIBAJ&pg=1286,587896&dq=i+don-t+want+to+spoil+the+illusion+of+snow+white&hl=en| access-date=January 5, 2013| newspaper=The Day| date=July 3, 1993| agency=Associated Press| location=New London CT}} After her work in Snow White, Caselotti tried a career in opera at the urging of her family. Her only role on the operatic stage was Gilda in [[Giuseppe Verdi|Verdi]]’s [[Rigoletto]], which she sang in 1944.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Ryan P. |title=Meet Adriana Caselotti, the voice of "Snow White" |url=http://www.mainstgazette.com/2009/09/meet-adriana-caselotti-voice-of-snow.html |access-date=2026-04-08}} It wasn’t a very successful affair, according to Caselotti herself. “I did Gilda in Rigoletto three times. First time, I had a cold. Second time, I was scared to death. Third time, I threw up backstage, and said, 'I'm going back to 'Snow White.’”{{Cite news |last=Chase |first=Chris |date=1983-07-22 |title=AT THE MOVIES |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1983/07/22/movies/at-the-movies.html |access-date=2026-04-07 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Caselotti also had several more jobs in the film business afterwards. The two most well-known were an uncredited role in MGM's ''[[The Wizard of Oz]]'' (1939) as the voice of [[Juliet]] during the Tin Woodman's song "If I Only Had a Heart", speaking the line "Wherefore art thou Romeo?"{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary-adriana-caselotti-1277975.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714053636/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary-adriana-caselotti-1277975.html |archive-date=2011-07-14 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |title=Obituary: Adriana Caselotti |last=Sibley |first=Brian |date=February 10, 1997 |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |access-date=October 8, 2017}} and an uncredited role in [[Frank Capra]]'s ''[[It's a Wonderful Life]]'' (1946), singing in Martini's bar as [[James Stewart]] is praying.{{cite web | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-dec-23-et-wonderful23-story.html| title=On a Wing and a Prayer| website=Los Angeles Times| date=November 24, 2022}} Adriana Caselotti appeared in several promotional spots for ''Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'' and signed memorabilia during promotional events. On November 22, 1972 ([[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving Day]]), she guest-starred on an episode of ''[[The Julie Andrews Hour]]'' saluting the music of Walt Disney, singing "I'm Wishing" and "[[Some Day My Prince Will Come]]" with [[Julie Andrews]].{{cite web| url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/heartbreaking-story-woman-played-disneys-180945993.html| title=The Heartbreaking Story of the Woman Who Played Disney's Snow White| website=Yahoo News| date=December 29, 2022}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} She also made a guest appearance on the syndicated ''[[The Mike Douglas Show]]''. Caselotti later wrote a how-to book, ''Do You Like to Sing?''. In the early 1990s, when the Snow White Grotto at [[Disneyland]] was refurbished, Caselotti, at the age of 75, re-recorded "I'm Wishing" for the Snow White Wishing Well exhibit. In 1994, she was named a [[Disney Legends|Disney Legend]]. She also sold autographs in her later years. ==Personal life== Caselotti was married four times. Her first husband was Robert James Chard, a local theater ticket broker[https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/16165259/ "The Bradford Era"]; ''Newspapers.com''; On-line Newspaper archives; article; Thursday, July 18, 1946; Bradford, Pennsylvania; p. 5; retrieved April 2021 whom she married in 1945. The marriage ended in divorce. She later met actor Norval Weir Mitchell, whom she married in 1952. He retired after marrying her and died in 1972. The same year, she was married to a podiatrist, Joseph Dana Costigan, who died in 1982.{{cite web | url=https://www.ocregister.com/2011/10/31/snow-whites-house-on-the-market-for-995000/| title=Snow White's House on the Market for $995,000| website=Orange Country Register| date=January 17, 2023}} Caselotti married her last husband, Joseph Laureat Florian St. Pierre, a retired postal employee, in 1989 and they later divorced. ==Death== Caselotti died of cancer at her Los Angeles home on January 19, 1997, at the age of 80. ==Filmography== ===Television=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
