''[[December Bride]]'' (1952–53; on radio) (1954–59; on television) | birth_name = Verna Arline Felton | spouse = {{marriage|Lee Carson Millar Sr. |1923|1941|end=died}} | children = 1 }} '''Verna Arline Felton''' (July 20, 1890{{spaced ndash}}December 14, 1966) was an American actress known for voicing characters in several classic [[Walt Disney Animation Studios|Disney]] animated films, including [[Fairy Godmother (Disney)|the Fairy Godmother]] in [[Cinderella (1950 film)|''Cinderella'']] (1950), the [[Queen of Hearts (Disney)|Queen of Hearts]] in [[Alice in Wonderland (1951 film)|''Alice in Wonderland'']] (1951), and [[Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather|Flora]] in [[Sleeping Beauty (1959 film)|''Sleeping Beauty'']] (1959). She also provided the voice for Fred Flintstone's mother-in-law, Pearl Slaghoople in [[Hanna-Barbera]]'s ''[[The Flintstones]]'' (1962–63) and had roles in live-action films. However, she was most active in radio programs, where her characters were known for their husky voices and no-nonsense attitudes. Two of her most famous roles were as Dennis Day's mother, Mrs. Day on both radio and television versions of ''[[The Jack Benny Program]]'' (1939–62) and as Hilda Crocker on ''[[December Bride]]'' (1952–59). Felton's television appearances included ''[[The George Burns and Gracie Allen Show]]'', ''[[I Love Lucy]]'', ''[[Where's Raymond?]]'', ''[[Pete and Gladys]]'' and ''[[Dennis the Menace (1959 TV series)|Dennis the Menace]]''. ==Early years== Verna Arline Felton was born in [[Salinas, California]], on July 20, 1890. Her father, Horace Wilcox Felton, a doctor, died shortly before her ninth birthday. When going over his accounts after his death, Felton's mother Clara Winder Felton (née Lawrence) discovered that although her husband had a large medical practice in [[San Jose, California|San Jose]], there were no records of his patients' payments for treatment and no cash in the office.{{Cite web |last=Nesteroff |first=Greg |date=2018-11-12 |title=Verna Felton in Nelson |url=https://www.kutnereader.com/post/verna-felton-in-nelson |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=Kutne Reader |language=en}} Shortly before her father's death, Felton had performed in a local benefit for victims of the [[1900 Galveston hurricane|Galveston Flood]]. Her singing and dancing attracted the attention of a manager of a road show company that was playing in San Jose at the time. The manager spoke to Felton's mother, offering to give Felton a job with his company. Since the family was experiencing difficult financial times with the loss of Felton's father, her mother contacted the road show manager. Felton quickly joined the cast of the show, growing up in the theater.{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/stream/radi00mac#page/n57/mode/2up|title=Love That Red-Head|author=Felton, Verna|publisher=Radio Mirror|date=January 1948|pages=46, 81, 82|access-date=May 18, 2014}} ==Early career== [[File:Stage juvenile Verna Felton (SAYRE 251).jpg|thumb|Felton in 1903]] An August 19, 1900, newspaper advertisement for Fischer's Concert House in San Francisco listed among the performers "Little Verna Felton, the Child Wonder."{{cite news |title=Fischer's Concert House ad |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28194550/the_san_francisco_call/ |access-date=February 9, 2019 |work=San Francisco Call |date=August 19, 1900 |location=California, San Francisco |page=35|via = [[Newspapers.com]]}} By 1903, she was acting with the Allen Stock Company,{{cite news |title=The Allen Stock Company |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28194928/verna_felton/ |access-date=February 9, 2019 |work=Petaluma Daily Morning Courier |date=February 2, 1903 |location=California, Petaluma |page=3|via = [[Newspapers.com]]}} which that year toured the [[West Coast of the United States]] and performed in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia, Canada.{{cite news |title=The People's Theatre |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28195220/the_province/ |access-date=February 9, 2019 |work=The Province |date=November 30, 1903 |location=Canada, British Columbia, Vancouver |page=8|via = [[Newspapers.com]]}} By 1907, she was still with the Allen troupe, but she had progressed from child performer to leading lady.{{cite news |title=At the Stock Theatres |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28195697/the_oregon_daily_journal/ |access-date=February 9, 2019 |work=The Oregon Daily Journal |date=May 7, 1907 |location=Oregon, Portland |page=5|via = [[Newspapers.com]]}} Herbert Bashford wrote a play, ''The Defiance of Doris'', specifically for Felton, and the Allen company included it among the group's productions in 1910.{{cite news |title=The Defiance of Doris |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28196232/verna_felton/ |access-date=February 9, 2019 |work=The Leader-Post |date=December 19, 1910 |location=Canada, Saskatchewan, Regina |page=3|via = [[Newspapers.com]]}} She acted in stage plays at the Empress Theatre in Vancouver in the late 1920s, playing the lead role in ''Goldfish'', ''Stella Dallas'', and ''The Second Mrs. Tanqueray''.{{Cite web|url=http://www.playford-beaudet.com/under-the-floorboards/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409044256/http://www.playford-beaudet.com/under-the-floorboards/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=April 9, 2018|title=Verna Felton, a brief introduction|last=Playford-Beaudet|first=Laurance|date=March 25, 2018|website=playford-beaudet.com|others=grunt gallery, Vancouver BC|via=posters from theatre}} Future husband Lee Millar (1888–1941) directed the band for these plays.{{Citation needed |date=September 2023}} ==Radio and TV== [[File:Skelton card 1948.jpg|thumb|left|''Raleigh Cigarettes Program'' 1948 cast: Standing: Pat McGeehan, [[The Four Knights]], [[David Rose (musician)|David Rose]] (orchestra leader). Seated: Verna Felton ("Grandma" to Skelton's "Junior" character), Rod O'Connor (announcer), [[Lurene Tuttle]] ("Mother" to Skelton's "Junior" character). Front: [[Red Skelton]].]] [[File:Harry Morgan Cara Williams Verna Felton Pete and Gladys 1960.JPG|thumb|left|[[Harry Morgan]], [[Cara Williams]] and Felton in ''[[Pete and Gladys]]'' (1960)]] Felton worked in the 1930s and 1950s in radio, including playing the children's mother on the serial ''[[The Cinnamon Bear]]'', Junior the Mean Widdle Kid's grandmother on [[Red Skelton]]'s radio series, Hattie Hirsch on ''Point Sublime'', and [[Dennis Day]]'s mother, Mrs. Day, who was always looking out for him while trying to boss around [[Jack Benny]] on ''[[The Jack Benny Program]]''. She recurred on ''[[The Great Gildersleeve]]'' and was heard on ''[[The Abbott and Costello Show (radio program)|The Abbott and Costello Show]]'' and other comedy shows, as well as dramatic roles on ''[[The Lux Radio Theatre]]''. She played the fairy godmother in one-shot adaptations of the [[Cinderella]] story on the anthology series ''[[Screen Directors Playhouse]]'' and ''[[Hallmark Playhouse]]''. Felton's first television appearance was in a 1951 episode of ''[[The Amos 'n Andy Show]]'' as a nurse. She appeared in a recurring role as the mother of Ruth Farley, a young woman played by [[Gloria Winters]] in the 1953–55 [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] sitcom with a variety show theme, ''[[Where's Raymond?]]'', renamed ''[[Where's Raymond?|The Ray Bolger Show]]''. Though some sitcom aficionados might assume that her guest appearances on ''[[I Love Lucy]]'' led to a regular supporting role as Hilda Crocker on the [[Columbia Broadcasting System|CBS]] sitcom ''[[December Bride]]'', Felton had played that same character on the radio version two years prior to the television production. Felton continued her Hilda Crocker role on the ''December Bride'' [[Spin-off (media)|spin-off]], ''[[Pete and Gladys]]'', with Harry Morgan and [[Cara Williams]]. For her performance on ''December Bride'', Felton was nominated for the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series]] in 1958 and 1959.{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1873&dat=19590418&id=m6YoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=DcoEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1979,3137261|title = Daytona Beach Morning Journal - Google News Archive Search}} Felton was the original voice of Fred Flintstone's mother-in-law, Pearl Slaghoople, voicing the character as a semi-regular in seasons two and three of [[Hanna-Barbera]]'s landmark TV series ''[[The Flintstones]]''. Fred's mother-in-law was not named during Felton's run; the "Slaghoople" name was mentioned in season four when [[Janet Waldo]] debuted in the role. In 1963, in the series finale of CBS's ''[[Dennis the Menace (1959 TV series)|Dennis the Menace]]'' sitcom, Felton played John Wilson's aunt in the episode entitled "Aunt Emma Visits the Wilsons". In the story line, Mr. Wilson ([[Gale Gordon]]) tries to convince Aunt Emma to leave her estate to him and his wife, Eloise ([[Sara Seegar]]). Wilson becomes suspicious when Emma begins spending time with Dennis Mitchell ([[Jay North]]). Felton's son Lee Millar Jr. played Tommy Anderson's father on the same sitcom. ==Film and animation== Felton's first on-screen appearance was in the 1917 silent film, ''The Chosen Prince, or The Friendship of David and Jonathan''. During the 1940s and the early 1950s, she was in demand as a character actress in films, with roles in ''[[If I Had My Way (film)|If I Had My Way]]'' (1940), ''[[Girls of the Big House]]'' (1945), ''[[The Fuller Brush Man]]'' (1948),'' [[Buccaneer's Girl]]'' (1950), ''[[Belles on Their Toes (film)|Belles on Their Toes]]'', ''[[Don't Bother to Knock]]'' (both 1952), and her memorable role as Mrs. Potts warmly acting as surrogate mother to [[William Holden]] in the 1955 [[picnic (1955 film)|film adaptation]] of [[William Inge]]'s stage play ''[[Picnic (play)|Picnic]]''. Felton was a popular actress at the [[The Walt Disney Company|Walt Disney Studios]], lending her voice to the animated features: *''[[Dumbo]]'' (1941) as the Elephant Matriarch and Mrs. Jumbo, Dumbo's Mother *''[[Cinderella (1950 film)|Cinderella]]'' (1950) as [[Fairy Godmother (Disney)|The Fairy Godmother]] *''[[Alice in Wonderland (1951 film)|Alice in Wonderland]]'' (1951) as the [[Queen of Hearts (Disney)|Queen of Hearts]] *''[[Lady and the Tramp]]'' (1955) as Aunt Sarah, Jim Dear's aunt (Felton's son voiced Jim Dear and the dogcatcher) *''[[Sleeping Beauty (1959 film)|Sleeping Beauty]]'' (1959) as [[Flora, Fauna and Merryweather|Flora]], the red fairy *''[[The Jungle Book (1967 film)|The Jungle Book]]'' (1967) as Winifred the elephant (posthumous release, her final role, animated or live-action) According to the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', Felton served as Honorary Mayor of [[North Hollywood, Los Angeles|North Hollywood]] for several years. ==Death== Felton died at her home of a [[stroke]] at the age of 76 on the evening of December 14, 1966, one day before [[Walt Disney]]'s death. Her final film, ''[[The Jungle Book]]'', was released in October 1967. She is interred at [[Grand View Memorial Park Cemetery]] in [[Glendale, California]].{{cite book |last1=Wilson |first1=Scott |title=Resting Places: The Burial Sites of More Than 14,000 Famous Persons, 3d ed. |date=19 August 2016 |publisher=McFarland |isbn=978-1-4766-2599-7 |page=238 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FOHgDAAAQBAJ&dq=%22on+TV+in+December+Bride+1954-59+%282+Emmy%22&pg=PA238 |access-date=November 21, 2021 |language=en}} ==Credits == ===Radio=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! '''Richard Durock''' (January 18, 1937 – September 17, 2009)<ref name="indiana">{{cite news |last1=Blasko |first1=Erin |title=South Bend Native, Actor Fondly Recalled |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-south-bend-tribune-dick-durock-1937/185739655/ |work=The South Bend Tribune |date=September 24, 2009 |location=South Bend, IN |page=B1 |access-date=November 27, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="ref2" /> was an American [[actor]] and [[Double (occupation)#Stunt double|stuntman]] who appeared in over eighty films and over seven hundred television episodes. He played the [[DC Comics]] superhero, [[Swamp Thing]], in both the feature films ''[[Swamp Thing (1982 film)|Swamp Thing]]'' (1982) and ''[[The Return of Swamp Thing]]'' (1989), and the 1990–1993 [[Swamp Thing (1990 TV series)|''Swamp Thing'' TV series]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/33729/rob-zombie-offers-updates-on-werewolf-women-of-the-s-s-and-tyrannosaurus-rex/|title=Rob Zombie Offers Updates on Werewolf Women of the S.S. and Tyrannosaurus Rex|last=unclecreepy|date=14 May 2012|website=Dread Central}}</ref> He stood an imposing 6'6".

== Biography ==
Durock played a rival Hulk-like creature on the television series ''[[The Incredible Hulk (1978 TV series)|The Incredible Hulk]]'', in a two-part episode titled "The First".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Incredible Hulk |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/enterprise-journal-dick-durock-1937-200/185686285/ |work=Enterprise-Journal |date=March 8, 1981 |location=McComb, MS |page=31 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Price |first1=Matthew |title=Swamp Thing Actor Relates Past Roles |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-oklahoman-dick-durock-1937-20/185686082/ |work=The Daily Oklahoman |date=January 25, 2008 |location=Oklahoma City, OK |page=77 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Durock also appeared in the Clint Eastwood films ''[[The Enforcer (1976 film)|The Enforcer]]'' (1976) and ''[[Any Which Way You Can]]'' (1980) as well as ''[[Doc Savage: The Man of Bronze]]'' (1975), and ''[[Falcon Crest]]'' in 1983 in the second-season finale as a henchman for The Cartel.  Durock also made a brief appearance in [[Rob Reiner]]'s film ''[[Stand by Me (film)|Stand by Me]]'' as a county fair pie-eating champion.

== Personal life ==
Durock was born in [[South Bend, Indiana]], to Serbian mother Sadie (Medich) and David Durock.<ref name="ref2">{{cite news|title=Richard Durock|publisher=South Bend Tribune|date=2009-09-24|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/southbendtribune/obituary.aspx?n=richard-durock&pid=133380233|access-date=2009-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UDZpAAAAMAAJ&q=%22ANOTHER+INDIANA+SERB+MAKES+IMPRESSIVE+STRIDES+IN+TELEVISION+AND+MOTION+PICTURES%22|title=Serb World|date=17 March 1982|publisher=Neven Publishing Corporation|via=Google Books}}</ref> He resided in [[Southern California]] and appeared at [[fan convention]]s.

== Death ==
Durock died of [[pancreatic cancer]] at his home in [[Oak Park, California]] on September 17, 2009. He was a veteran of the [[United States Marine Corps]].<ref name="indiana" />

{{Short description|New Zealand actor (1940–2012)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2016}} {{Use Australian English|date=September 2016}} {{Infobox person |name=Jonathan Hardy |image=Jonathan Hardy.gif |birth_date={{birth date|1940|9|20|df=yes}} |birth_place=[[Wellington]], [[New Zealand]] |death_date={{death date and age|2012|7|30|1940|9|20|df=yes}} |death_place=[[Southern Highlands (New South Wales)|Southern Highlands]], [[New South Wales]], Australia |education= New Zealand Players' Drama School
[[London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art]] |occupation=Actor, writer, director |years_active = 1966–2012 |partner= David Letch }} '''Jonathan Hardy''' (20 September 1940 – 30 July 2012) was a New Zealand-Australian film and television actor, writer and director.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/news/article.cfm?c_id=1501119&objectid=10823485|title=Kiwi actor Jonathan Hardy dies aged 71|date=31 July 2012|website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=19 August 2017}} ==Early life and education== Hardy was born in [[Wellington]], [[New Zealand]] on 20 September 1940, to cavalry officer Captain Burnby Hardy and Mary Hardy (nee Philpott). His father was killed by a sniper in [[Crete]] that same year, and his mother died when Hardy was only 19.{{Cite web |title= Jonathan Hardy: Actor, Writer |url= https://www.nzonscreen.com/profile/jonathan-hardy/biography |access-date=13 September 2025 |website= www.nzonscreen.com}} He began his training at the New Zealand Players' Drama School. He then traveled to Britain, where he studied at the [[London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art]] (LAMDA) and was a gold medal student.{{Cite web |last=Juddery |first=Mark |date=9 September 2012 |title=Versatile actor carved out a remarkable career |url=http://www.smh.com.au/comment/obituaries/versatile-actor-carved-out-a-remarkable-career-20120902-2587o.html |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}} He also spent time doing vocal study in Spain. ==Career== Hardy's acting career lasted for over 40 years, from 1966 to 2012. ===Theatre=== Hardy preferred to work on the stage. Following his studies in the UK, he attracted interest from the [[Royal Shakespeare Company]] and the [[Royal National Theatre]] where he secured contracts,{{Cite web |last=Juddery |first=Mark |date=9 September 2012 |title=Versatile actor carved out a remarkable career |url=http://www.smh.com.au/comment/obituaries/versatile-actor-carved-out-a-remarkable-career-20120902-2587o.html |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}} as well as the [[Bristol Old Vic]] and several regional theatres. He returned to his home in New Zealand in a touring production of ''[[The Comedy of Errors]]'' with the [[Royal Shakespeare Company]] in 1966, and remained to help expand the country's early theatre industry.{{cite news |date=31 July 2012 |title=ATC mourns actor Jonathan Hardy |newspaper=Voxy.co.nz |url=http://www.voxy.co.nz/entertainment/atc-mourns-actor-jonathan-hardy/5/130505 |access-date=1 August 2012}} Hardy relocated to Australia in 1972, but also returned to New Zealand regularly throughout the mid 1980s,{{cite web|url= https://thebigidea.nz/stories/tribute-jonathan-hardy |title= Tribute: Jonathan Hardy |website= www.thebigidea.nz |date= 31 July 2012}} to perform as a guest actor with [[Auckland Theatre Company]], including playing [[Willy Loman]] in a production of ''[[Death of a Salesman]]''. He headed the [[Melbourne Theatre Company|Melbourne Theatre Company’s]] youth wing for two years. In 1978 he appeared in the premiere stage production of [[Kenneth G. Ross]]'s Australian play ''[[Breaker Morant (play)|Breaker Morant]]'', presented by the [[Melbourne Theatre Company]] at the [[Melbourne Athenaeum|Athenaeum]] theatre, in [[Melbourne, Victoria, Australia]], on Thursday, 2 February 1978.{{Cite web |url=https://www.ausstage.edu.au/pages/event/5970 |title=Breaker Morant |website=[[AusStage]] |access-date=19 August 2017}} The play was subsequently adapted into a film, for which Hardy co-wrote the script, earning him a 1981 [[Academy Awards]] nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay. Hardy then became Artistic Director of Auckland's [[Mercury Theatre, Auckland|Mercury Theatre]], a role he undertook for five years. He also played [[Captain Ahab]] in ''[[Moby Dick—Rehearsed]]'' and appeared in [[Gallipoli]] saga ''Once on Chunuk Bair''. Hardy had long engagements with major theatre companies in both [[Melbourne]] and [[Sydney]]. His roles ranged from a Christmas pantomime of ''Cinderella'', [[Shakespeare]], opera and topical plays such as ''And in the End: The Life and Death of John Lennon''. In his obituary, he is quoted by [[Mark Juddery]] as saying, "The actor is in control in the theatre... so the theatre is much more an actor's medium" and "Television is not anything but an actor's image... If my image happens to fit, then I do the job. Whereas on stage you can create an illusion, on television… it's pretty cliched." ===Film=== Hardy appeared in over 20 films, guest-starred in over 26 television series, and acted in many television movies and miniseries.{{Cite web |title=Jonathan Hardy |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0362682/ |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=IMDb}} His early roles included the [[BBC]] children's time travel series ''[[Mandog]]'' in 1972, and a small role in the London-set Australian comedy feature ''[[The Adventures of Barry McKenzie]]'' that same year. His film work continued with the 1976 [[Fred Schepisi]] feature ''[[The Devil's Playground (1976 film)|The Devil's Playground]]'', for which he was nominated for an [[Australian Film Institute]] award. He also starred in [[George Miller (filmmaker)|George Miller]] dystopian action classic ''[[Mad Max (film)|Mad Max]]'' in 1979, and appeared in ''[[The Sullivans]]'' TV movie spin-off ''[[The Sullivans|The John Sullivan Story]]'' that same year.{{cite web|url= https://www.nzonscreen.com/profile/jonathan-hardy/screenography |title= Jonathan Hardy Screenography |website= www.nzonscreen.com |date= 18 September 2025}} At Italy's {{ill|MystFest|it|vertical-align=sup}}, Hardy was the co-winner of Best Artistic Contribution for his role in 1982 horror film ''[[The Scarecrow (1982 film)|Scarecrow]]''. He later appeared in ''[[Mr. Reliable]]'' aka ''My Entire Life'' (1996) alongside [[Colin Friels]] and [[Jacqueline McKenzie]], and the [[Baz Luhrmann]] musical epic ''[[Moulin Rouge!]]'' (2001), in which he played the character of the 'Man in the Moon', for whom [[Plácido Domingo]] supplied the singing voice. He won a [[New Zealand film and television awards|New Zealand Film and TV Award]] in 2001, for his performance in 2000 short film ''Camping with Camus''. He then appeared in the 2003 feature ''[[Ned Kelly]]'', opposite [[Heath Ledger]] and [[Orlando Bloom]], playing 'The Great Orlando'. Hardy became best known to international audiences for providing the voice of diminutive alien ex-royal leader [[Dominar Rygel XVI]] in the science fiction series ''[[Farscape]]'' from 1999 to 2003, and its subsequent 2004 made-for-television film ''[[Farscape: The Peacekeeper Wars]]''. ''Farscape'' was filmed in [[Sydney]], Australia, but was a United States production. Although the series was unsuccessful in Australia, Hardy developed a cult following and made appearances at sci-fi conventions. Hardy's other television roles include Josef Goldman in ''Twenty Good Years'' in 1979, and the miniseries' ''[[Power Without Glory]]'' (1976) ''The Mackenzie Affair'' (1977) and ''[[Against the Wind (miniseries)|Against the Wind]]'' (1978). He made guest appearances in numerous television series including ''[[Rush (1974 TV series)|Rush]]'', ''[[Bluey (1976 TV series)|Bluey]]'', ''[[Young Ramsay]]'', ''[[The Truckies]]'', ''[[The Sullivans]]'', ''[[Prisoner (TV series)|Prisoner]]'', ''[[Under the Mountain (miniseries)|Under the Mountain]]'', ''[[Butterfly Island]]'', ''[[Rafferty's Rules]]'', ''[[G.P.]]'', ''[[Mission: Impossible (1988 TV series)|Mission: Impossible]]'', ''[[E Street (TV series)|E Street]]'', ''[[The Flying Doctors]]'', ''[[A Country Practice]]'', ''[[The Adventures of Skippy]]'', ''[[Snowy River: The McGregor Saga]]'', ''[[Fire (TV series)|Fire]]'', ''[[Medivac (TV series)|Medivac]]'', ''[[Twisted Tales (Australian TV series)|Twisted Tales]]'', ''[[All Saints (TV series)|All Saints]]'', ''[[State Coroner (TV series)|State Coroner]]'', ''[[Above the Law (TV series)|Above the Law]]'', ''[[The Secret Life of Us]]'', ''[[Stingers (TV series)|Stingers]]'', ''[[MDA (TV series)|MDA]]'' and ''Magical Tales''. Along with [[David Stevens (screenwriter)|David Stevens]] and [[Bruce Beresford]], Hardy co-wrote the screenplay for the film ''[[Breaker Morant (film)|Breaker Morant]]'', for which he received an [[Australian Film Institute]] Award (1980), and was nominated for an [[Academy Award]] (1981).{{Cite web |title=Jonathan Hardy – Awards |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0362682/awards? |access-date=19 August 2017 |website=IMDb}} He also wrote and directed the movie ''[[Backstage (1988 film)|Backstage]]'', starring the [[Grammy]] nominated pop vocalist [[Laura Branigan]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094700/ |title=Backstage (1988) |website=IMDb |access-date=19 August 2017}} His screen directing career however, failed to take off. '''Lawrence Dobkin''' (September 16, 1919 – October 28, 2002) was an American [[television director]], character actor and [[television writer|screenwriter]] whose career spanned seven decades.

Dobkin was a prolific performer during the [[Old-time radio|Golden Age of Radio]]. He narrated the western ''[[Broken Arrow (1950 film)|Broken Arrow]]'' (1950). His film performances include ''[[Never Fear]]'' (1949), ''[[Sweet Smell of Success]]'' (1957), ''[[North by Northwest]]'' (1959) and ''[[Geronimo]]'' (1962). Before the closing credits of each episode of the  landmark [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television network series ''[[Naked City (TV series)|Naked City]]'' (1958–1963), he said, "There are eight million stories in the naked city.  This has been one of them."<ref name="Vallance2002">{{cite news| title=Obituary: Lawrence Dobkin: Prolific and Versatile Character Actor| work=[[The Independent]]| date=October 9, 2002| author=Vallance, Tom| location=London| url=http://www.saint.org/actor-lawrence-dobkin.htm| via=Saint.org}}</ref>

== Early years ==
Dobkin was born in [[Manhattan]], New York City to a Jewish family. His parents were Samuel Dobkin (1888–1948) and Frieda ({{née}} Feder, 1890–1984).<ref>{{cite web | title=Lawrence C Dobkin - Ancestry® | website=[[Ancestry.com]] | url=https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/lawrence-c-dobkin-24-57hy3v }}</ref> Dobkin served in a radio propaganda unit of the [[United States Army Air Forces|U.S. Army Air Forces]] during [[World War II]].<ref>[https://www.rusc.com/old-time-radio/Lawrence-Dobkin.aspx?t=234 Lawrence Dobkins] rusc.com. Retrieved May 13, 2023.</ref>

==Radio==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2023}}
Dobkin understudied on [[Broadway (theatre)|Broadway]].<ref name="slst">{{cite news |last1=Kimbrough |first1=Mary |title=Understudy Makes Good On Stage And In The Army |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21755046/lawrence_dobkin/ |newspaper=[[St. Louis Star-Times]] |date=November 1, 1943 |page=12 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date = July 10, 2018}}</ref> When he returned to network radio he was one of five actors who played the detective [[Ellery Queen]] in ''[[The Adventures of Ellery Queen (radio program)|The Adventures of Ellery Queen]]''.<ref name="opa"/> In ''[[The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe]]'' (1950–1951), Dobkin played detective [[Archie Goodwin (character)|Archie Goodwin]] opposite [[Sydney Greenstreet]]'s [[Nero Wolfe]].

While playing Louie, [[Simon Templar|"The Saint"]]'s cab-driving sidekick on [[NBC Radio]] in 1951, he was asked to step into the lead role of Simon Templar to replace [[Tom Conway]] for a single episode —  making Dobkin one of the many actors to portray [[Leslie Charteris]]' literary creation.<ref name="Saint.org">{{cite web| url=http://www.saint.org/actor-lawrence-dobkin.htm | title=Lawrence Dobkin (Larry Dobkin)| website=Saint.org| access-date=2013-06-27}}</ref>

Other radio work included ''[[Escape (radio program)|Escape]]'' (1947–1954); ''[[Gunsmoke]]'' (1952–1961); ''[[Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]]'' (1956–1960); and the anthology series ''[[Lux Radio Theater]]''. "The few of us who are left," Dobkin said of his radio days not long before he died, "keep telling each other that we never had it so good."<ref name="Vallance2002"/>

He played Lieutenant Matthews on ''[[The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]]'', along with several other characters. Continuing to work as a [[voice actor]] throughout his career, Dobkin contributed to the [[video game]] ''[[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear]]'' (1999).

==Television==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2023}}
Dobkin began a prolific career in television in 1946, having worked as an actor, narrator and director. In 1953, he guest-starred on [[Alan Hale, Jr.]]'s short-lived [[CBS]] espionage series set in the [[Cold War]], ''[[Biff Baker, U.S.A.]]''. He was cast in a 1957 episode of the [[Television syndication|syndicated]] series ''The Silent Service'', in "The Ordeal of the S 38", based on true stories of the [[submarine]] division of the [[United States Navy]], in which he was the lead actor and was credited incorrectly as Lawrence Bodkin. He appeared also in the religion [[anthology series]], ''[[Crossroads (1955 TV series)|Crossroads]]'', based on experiences of American [[clergy]]men, and later on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] religion drama, ''[[Going My Way (TV series)|Going My Way]]'', starring [[Gene Kelly]].

In the 1950s [[situation comedy]] ''[[I Love Lucy]]'' Dobkin played the roles of "Restaurant Man" in episode 66 ("Ricky and Fred Are TV Fans"), "Waiter" in episode 70 ("Equal Rights"), and "Counterfeiter" in episode 145 ("Paris at Last").<ref name=nite>{{cite book| title=Nick at Nite's Classic TV Companion| editor-first=Tom| editor-last=Hill| year=1996| publisher=Simon & Schuster| pages=264, 266, 289| url=https://archive.org/details/nickatnitesclass00hill/page/264/mode/2up?q=Dobkin| isbn=978-0-6848-1593-0}}</ref>

In the 1957-1958 television season, Dobkin played a director on the [[CBS]] [[sitcom]], ''[[Mr. Adams and Eve]]'', starring [[Howard Duff]] and [[Ida Lupino]] as fictitious married actors residing in [[Beverly Hills, California|Beverly Hills]], [[California]]. He guest-starred in 1958 in the first season of ABC's ''[[The Donna Reed Show]]''.

In 1957, Dobkin appeared in the third episode of the first season of the CBS Television western ''[[Have Gun – Will Travel]]'',  entitled "The Great Mohave Chase",  as the owner of water rights in the small western town of Mohave.

In the May 9, 1958 episode of the CBS Television western series ''[[Trackdown (TV series)|Trackdown]]'' entitled, "The End of the World", he portrays a con man named Walter Trump who promises to save a town from destruction by building a wall.

In 1960, Dobkin appeared as Kurt Reynolds in the episode "So Dim the Light" of the CBS [[anthology series]] ''[[The DuPont Show with June Allyson]]'', and as an escape artist on the run from a possible murder charge in ''[[Wanted: Dead or Alive (TV series)|Wanted: Dead or Alive]]''. That same year he played "Esteban Garcia" (a long time friend of Marshal Dillon where things go very wrong) in the TV Western ''[[Gunsmoke]]'', in the episode "Don Matteo" (S6E7). He appeared in the [[David Janssen]] crime drama series, ''[[Richard Diamond, Private Detective]]''. Dobkin appeared in four episodes of ''[[The Rifleman]]'' playing four different characters, including a heartfelt portrayal of General [[Philip Sheridan]] from the [[American Civil War]]. He appeared in an episode of ''[[The Tab Hunter Show]]'' in 1961. In 1964 he narrated the USIS documentary film about the Republican and Democrat conventions called "1964 The Conventions."

Often also cast as a villain, Dobkin portrayed [[gangster]] [[Dutch Schultz]] on ABC's ''[[The Untouchables (1959 TV series)|The Untouchables]]''. He appeared on the ABC/[[Warner Bros.]] crime drama, ''[[The Roaring 20s (TV series)|The Roaring 20s]]'' and in the [[NBC]] western with a modern setting, ''[[Empire (1962 TV series)|Empire]]''. He was cast as a mass murderer in the 1972 pilot for ABC's ''[[The Streets of San Francisco]]'', starring [[Karl Malden]]. He guest-starred on ABC's ''[[The Big Valley]]'', starring [[Barbara Stanwyck]].<ref name="Erickson">{{cite web | url=http://www.allmovie.com/artist/lawrence-dobkin-p87920 | title=Lawrence Dobkin | publisher=All Movie | access-date=2013-06-27 | author=Erickson, Hal}}</ref> He received an [[Emmy Award]] nomination for Outstanding Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role in a Drama for his work on the ''[[CBS Playhouse]]'' episode, ''[[Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night (CBS Playhouse)|Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night]]'' (1967).<ref>{{cite web |title=Lawrence Dobkin |url=http://www.emmys.com/awards/nominations/award-search?search_api_views_fulltext=Lawrence+Dobkin&submit=Search&field_celebrity_details_field_display_name=&field_show_details_field_nominee_show_nr_title=&field_show_details_field_network=All&field_show_details_field_production_company=All&field_nominations_year=1949-01-01+00%3A00%3A00&field_nominations_year_1=2018-01-01+00%3A00%3A00&field_award_category=All |website=Academy of Television Arts & Sciences |access-date=11 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411073759/http://www.emmys.com/bios/lawrence-dobkin |archive-date=April 11, 2016}}</ref> In 1991, Dobkin appeared in an episode of the television series ''[[Night Court]]'' as State Supreme Court Justice Welch.

In the ''[[Star Trek]]'' media franchise Dobkin directed the [[Star Trek: The Original Series|original series]] episode "[[Charlie X]]", and later portrayed the traitorous [[Klingon]] ambassador Kell on ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'' in the fourth-season episode [[The Mind's Eye (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|"The Mind's Eye"]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The Star Trek Encyclopedia|first1=Michael|last1=Okuda|first2=Denise|last2=Okuda|publisher=[[Pocket Books]]|year=1994|pages=47, 152|url=https://archive.org/details/startrekencycl00okud/mode/2up?q=dobkin|isbn=978-0-6718-8684-4}}</ref>

As a writer, Dobkin created the title character for the 1974 film and the 1977–1978 NBC series ''[[The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams]]''.

He began directing for television in 1960, and his work in this area included episodes 1, 9, 10, and 13 of ''[[The Munsters]]'' (1964),<ref>{{cite book|title=Nick at Nite's Classic TV Companion|pages=358–359, 361–363|quote=The episodes are numbered in the order they were broadcast which is not the same order in which they were filmed which notes that episode 2 was actually made first}}</ref> 16 episodes of ''[[The Waltons]]'' (1972–1981), and an episode of ''[[Sara (U.S. 1976 TV series)|Sara]]'' (1976). Dobkin also guest-starred on a 1983 episode of ''[[Knight Rider]]''.

==Films==
Dobkin's notable supporting film roles include ''[[Twelve O'Clock High]]'' (1949), ''[[The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951 film)|The Day the Earth Stood Still]]'' (1951),  ''[[Julius Caesar (1953 film)|Julius Caesar]]'' (1953), ''[[The Ten Commandments (1956 film)|The Ten Commandments]]'' (1956), ''[[The Defiant Ones (film)|The Defiant Ones]]'' (1958), ''[[Johnny Yuma (film)|Johnny Yuma]]'' (1966) and ''[[Patton (film)|Patton]]'' (1970). He had a cameo appearance in the 1954 sci-fi thriller ''[[Them!|Them]]''. In an uncredited performance in Alfred Hitchcock's ''[[North by Northwest]]'', Dobkin has a memorable line as an intelligence official who remarks on the plight of the hapless protagonist, on the run for murder after being mistaken for a person who doesn't exist: "It's so horribly sad. Why is it I feel like laughing?" {{Citation needed|date=February 2013}}

==Personal life==
On June 24, 1961, Dobkin married the actress [[Joanna Barnes]];<ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Dobkin, Joanna Barnes Marry |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/los-angeles-evening-citizen-news-lawrenc/191123436/ |work=Los Angeles Evening Citizen News |date=June 26, 1961 |location=Hollywood, CA |page=4 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Joanna Barnes Wed to Lawrence Dobkin |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-blade-lawrence-dobkin-1919-2002/191123503/ |work=The Blade |date=June 26, 1961 |location=Toledo, OH |page=3 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> they had no children,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Dobkin Wants Divorce |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-houston-post-lawrence-dobkin-1919-2/191123532/ |work=The Houston Post |date=August 21, 1966 |location=Houston, TX |page=64 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> but he had one daughter, Debra Dobkin, by his first wife, Frances Hope Walker. Dobkin married the actress Anne Collings in 1970 and had two children: identical twin daughters, Kristy and Kaela.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

==Death==
On October 28, 2002, Dobkin died of heart failure at age 83 at his Los Angeles home.<ref name="opa">{{cite book |last1=Lentz |first1=Harris M. III |title=Obituaries in the Performing Arts, 2002: Film, Television, Radio, Theatre, Dance, Music, Cartoons and Pop Culture |date=2003 |publisher=McFarland |isbn=978-0-7864-5207-1 |pages=84–85 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Z3rGCwAAQBAJ&q=%22Lawrence+Dobkin%22&pg=PA84 |access-date=July 11, 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Mihaly''' "'''Michu'''" '''Meszaros''' ([[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]: '''Mészáros Mihály''', {{ipa|hu|ˈmeːsaːroʃ ˈmihaːj}}; 1 October 1939 – 12 June 2016)<ref name=telegraphobit/> was a Hungarian and American actor, circus performer/entertainer, and stuntman. He was {{convert|2|ft|9|in|m}} tall and weighed 25 pounds.<ref name=breezeobit/> He was best remembered as a performer with [[Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus]] and for his role in the [[NBC]] sitcom ''[[ALF (TV series)|ALF]]'' in 1986. He appeared in many films in the late 1980s and early 1990s and also appeared opposite [[Michael Jackson]] in a [[Pepsi]] commercial<ref name=nolaobit/> and in the [[Ozzy Osbourne]] music video for "[[No More Tears|Time After Time]]" in 1992. His last appearance was in ''Death to Cupid'' (2015).

==Biography==
===Early life===
Meszaros was born in a small village outside [[Budapest]] and was the seventh of nine siblings.<ref name=breezeobit>{{Cite news | url=https://www.dailybreeze.com/2016/06/13/michu-meszaros-33-inch-tall-circus-performer-and-actor-who-played-alf-dies-in-torrance/ | title='Michu' Meszaros, 33-inch-tall circus performer and actor who played 'Alf' dies in Torrance | first=Larry | last=Altman | work=[[Daily Breeze]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref> He attended a school of circus arts and performed in the circus since age nine, working two or three shows a day, five days a week.<ref name=breezeobit/> He performed in the Liebel Family Circus and toured Eastern Europe.<ref name=legacy/> However, a government agent from the [[Hungarian People's Republic]] followed him to make sure he did not [[Defection|defect]], and the government took most of his money.<ref name=breezeobit/>

===Career===
Circus producers [[Irvin Feld]] and [[Kenneth Feld]] had heard of Meszaros, and, after locating him in 1973, signed him to a contract and made arrangements to bring him to the U.S. and have him star in the [[Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus]] as the "smallest man in the world".<ref name=telegraphobit>{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2016/07/01/mihaly-michu-meszaros-smallest-man--obituary/ | title=Mihaly 'Michu' Meszaros, 'smallest man' – obituary |  work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | date=1 July 2016 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=nolaobit>{{Cite web | url=https://obits.nola.com/us/obituaries/nola/name/michu-meszaros-obituary?pid=180327059 | title=Michu Meszaros Obituary | work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]] | date=June 14, 2016 | via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>

In 1980, Meszaros, along with his Hungarian guard, defected to the U.S.<ref name=breezeobit/> He became a [[resident alien]] in 1984.<ref name=breezeobit/>

As a circus performer, he performed an act with [[poodle]]s, in which the poodles, standing on their hind legs, appeared much taller than Meszaros, delighting children in the crowd.<ref name=nolaobit/>

In the Grand Spectacle performance of 1982 and 1983, Meszaros portrayed a character known as the Marshal of Marshmallow Gulch, resplendent in a well-tailored white, silver and gold costume encrusted with [[rhinestone]]s, along with a ten-gallon [[cowboy hat]] and silver [[cowboy boot]]s.<ref name=telegraphobit/>

In the 1980s, [[Hawthorne, California]], where he resided, named the shortest street in that city "Michu Lane" in his honor.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/1987/06/13/a-street-called-michu/ | title=A Street Called Michu | work=[[The Sun Sentinel]] | location=Ft. Lauderdale | date=13 June 1987 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=breezeobit/>

For the first season of the ''[[ALF (TV series)|ALF]]'' television series, in 1986, Meszaros donned a costume whenever a full-body shot was needed for scenes of the alien walking, running, or standing. However, in most cases, upper-body shots of a mechanical puppet were used instead as the costume was uncomfortable. Meszaros had no lines in the show and was let go after two years.<ref name=breezeobit/>

Meszaros became a U.S. citizen in 1990.<ref name=breezeobit/><ref name=hrobit>{{Cite news | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/michu-meszaros-dead-alf-actor-902332/ | title=Michu Meszaros, Who Played the Alien ALF on TV, Dies at 76 | first=Mike | last=Barnes | work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref>

==Death==
Meszaros died in June 2016 at Providence Little Company of Mary Medical Center in [[Torrance, California]], after a [[stroke]] at his home that left him in a coma for several days. He had overcome another stroke eight years earlier and was dealing with several health issues.<ref name=breezeobit/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cnn.com/2016/06/13/entertainment/alf-actor-dies/index.html | last=Melas | first=Chloe  | title=Mihaly 'Michu' Meszaros, actor who played 'ALF,' dies at 76 | work=[[CNN]] | date=13 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.brainerddispatch.com/lifestyle/arts-and-entertainment/alf-actor-michu-meszaros-dies-at-76 | title='Alf' Actor Michu Meszaros Dies at 76 | agency=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | work=[[Brainerd Dispatch]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref><ref name=legacy>{{Cite web | url=https://www.legacy.com/news/celebrity-deaths/notable-deaths/article/michu-meszaros-1939-2016?preview=7305531 | title=Michu Meszaros Obituary | work=[[Legacy.com]] | date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

In October 2018, his memorial service was held at the [[Dearly Departed Tours & Artifact Museum]], owned and operated by author and historian Scott Michaels. Meszaros’ remains had been inurned and on public display along with items from his life and career until the museum closed in 2021. In September 2023, a crowdfunding campaign was launched by Michaels and "Dearly Departed", in order to raise funds for a  formal, more appropriate interment.<ref>{{Cite AV media | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c_vVb9KqOKE | title=The Little Man Inside ALF is Unburied - Michael Jackson's Best Man! | date=September 7, 2023 | via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> This was successful, and Meszaros was ultimately interred at [[Valhalla Memorial Park]] in April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=travsd |date=2024-04-05 |title=This Friday in Hollywood: Michu Gets Memorialized |url=https://travsd.wordpress.com/2024/04/05/this-friday-in-hollywood-michu-gets-memorialized/ |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=(Travalanche) |language=en}}</ref>

{{short description|Mexican professional wrestler and actor}} {{about|the wrestler|the TV series|Blue Demon (TV series)|the 2004 film|Blue Demon (film)}} {{missing information|more detail on the person's life, and career|date=April 2018}} {{Use mdy dates|date=February 2019}} {{Infobox person | name = Blue Demon | birth_name = Alejandro Muñoz Moreno | image = Luchador Blue Demon en Blue Demon y las invasoras (1969).jpg | caption = Blue Demon in ''Blue Demon y las invasoras'' (1969) | birth_date = {{birth date|1922|10|12}} | birth_place = [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico | children = [[Blue Demon Jr.]] (adopted) | spouse = Gregoria Moreno | death_date = {{death date and age|2000|12|16|1922|4|24}} | death_place = [[Mexico City]], Mexico | burial_place = Parque Memorial Gayosso
[[Naucalpan|Naucalpan de Juárez]] | module = {{Infobox professional wrestler | child=yes | ring_names = {{Unbulleted list|Tosco Muñoz|Blue Demon ("Demonio Azul"){{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=3217|title=Blue Demon|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=Cagematch.net}}}} | height = {{convert|1.69|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} | weight = {{convert|77|kg|lb|abbr=on}} | trainer = [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] | debut = March 31, 1948 | retired = August 27, 1989 }} }} '''Alejandro Muñoz Moreno''' (October 12, 1922 – December 16, 2000), better known by the [[ring name]] '''Blue Demon''' (''Demonio Azul'' in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]), was a Mexican film [[actor]] and [[professional wrestler]]. Blue Demon is considered a legend of [[professional wrestling in Mexico]], partially from starring in a series of ''[[Lucha films]]'' between 1961 and 1979, often alongside in-ring rival [[El Santo]]. His in-ring career began in 1948 and stretched for 41 years until his retirement in 1989. Throughout his career Muñoz never lost a ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' match and retired without exposing his face to the public; he would later be buried in his signature blue and silver mask. In his 41-year career he won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] twice, the [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship]] three times and the [[Mexican National Tag Team Championship]] with long time tag team partner [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]]. He also won the hair of [[Cavernario Galindo]] and the masks of Espectro II, Matemático, and most notably, the mask of [[Rayo de Jalisco Sr.|Rayo de Jalisco]]. Near the end of his career Muñoz introduced [[Blue Demon Jr.]] to the wrestling world, who despite being promoted as the son of Blue Demon, did not actually share a blood connection to Muñoz; he was later claimed to be the "adopted son". Muñoz's actual son owns the trademarks to the name "Blue Demon", while Blue Demon Jr. owns the trademark to the "Blue Demon Jr." name. [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) honors the legacy of Blue Demon by holding the ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament at irregular intervals. He was chosen for the [[Wrestling Observer Newsletter Hall of Fame]] by Dave Meltzer in 1996 as part of the inaugural HOF selection. ==Early life== {{Professional wrestling sidebar}}Alejandro Muñoz Moreno was born October 12, 1922, in [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre& honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Los Enmascarados (the masked men): El Demonio Azul (the Blue Demon) | pages = 79–90| isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} He was the child of farmers and was the fifth of twelve children. At a young age, Alejandro dropped out of school and moved to [[Monterrey]], where his uncle gave him a job working on the [[Ferrocarriles Nacionales de México|National Railroad]]. His co-workers gave him the nickname 'Manotas', referring to his large, powerful hands.{{cite book|author=Harris M. Lentz III|title=Obituaries in the Performing Arts, 2000: Film, Television, Radio, Theatre, Dance, Music, Cartoons and Pop Culture|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XjGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA28|date=June 1, 2001|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-0-7864-1024-8|pages=28}} ==Professional wrestling career== A chance meeting with the famous Mexican wrestler [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] piqued his interest in [[Lucha Libre]], Vera even offering to tutor him and help him start a career. He began wrestling without a mask in [[Laredo, Texas]]. His first match was against Chema Lopez on March 12, 1948. Adopting the mask and persona of The Blue Demon, he headed back to Mexico to start a full-time in-ring career. His first appearance as The Blue Demon was in [[Mexico City]] in September 1948, where he fought Benny Arcilla. Blue Demon began his career in the ring as a [[Heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]] (a bad guy).{{cite book | author= Various | title= Lucha Libre: Masked Superstars of Mexican Wrestling | publisher= Distributed Art Publishers, Inc. | year= 2005 | chapter = El Demonio Azul / Blue Demon | pages = 162–186| isbn=968-6842-48-9}} {{cite news | author = L.L. Staff | title = Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero | work = Blue Demon (1922 - 2000) | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | page = 11 | year = 2008|language = es}} From there, he formed a tag team with another masked [[Lucha libre|luchador]] named The Black Shadow, and the two became known as ''Los Hermanos Shadow'' (The Shadow Brothers). In 1952, the famous wrestler [[El Santo]] beat and unmasked [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]] in the ring, which triggered Blue's decision to become a [[Face (professional wrestling)|técnico]] (a good guy) in the ring, and a legendary feud between Blue Demon and El Santo was started. The storyline feud between the two culminated with Blue Demon defeating El Santo in a well-publicized series of matches in 1952 and 1953. In 1953, Blue won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] from Santo, and held it until 1958. Their rivalry never entirely abated in later years (although they co-starred in a number of Mexican horror films) since Santo always remembered his defeat at the Blue Demon's hands. During the 1960s, one of Blue Demon's rivals was el Rayo de Jalisco. In 1988, the year he retired, Blue Demon defeated Jalisco in a [[Professional wrestling match types#Luchas de apuestas|mask vs. mask match]], taking the mask of another of Mexico's wrestling legends.John F. Molinaro, ''The Top 100 Pro Wrestlers of All Time'', (Winding Stair Press: 2002), page 195.{{cite news | author = Enciclopedia staff | title = Enciclopedia de las Mascaras | work = Rayo de Jalisco | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Tomo IV | page = 6 | date = October 2007| language = es}} Blue Demon retired from the ring in 1989, aged 67, at the [[Monterrey Arena]], where he appeared in a final match, teaming up with his adoptive son, [[Blue Demon Jr.]] ==Acting career== Blue Demon first appeared in cameos in a couple of [[lucha film|luchador films]] released in 1961–1962, "The Killers of Lucha Libre" and "Fury in the Ring", in which he was one of several wrestlers more or less in the background. But in 1964, Enrique Vergara, the producer of the then-successful Santo movies, decided to diversify by allowing the 42-year-old Blue Demon to star in a series of luchador films of his own. The plots of the Blue Demon films are thought to be extremely similar to those of Santo's films. Santo was asking for a salary increase at the time and Vergara wanted to cultivate a second movie star.{{cite book|author=Robert Cotter|title=The Mexican Masked Wrestler and Monster Filmography|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C7rwCQAAQBAJ&pg=PA96|date=April 21, 2008|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0419-0|pages=96}}{{cite book|author=Doyle Greene|title=Mexploitation Cinema: A Critical History of Mexican Vampire, Wrestler, Ape-Man and Similar Films, 1957–1977|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ci1zBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA86|date=May 29, 2012|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0072-7|pages=85–86}} From 1964 to 1979, Blue Demon starred in a total of 25 action/horror/science fiction films. Of those 25 films, Santo co-starred with him in nine of them. In three of his films, Blue Demon starred as the leader of a squadron of masked superheroes known as ''Los Campeones Justicieros'' (The Champions of Justice). Membership in the Champions included such legendary Mexican wrestling figures as Blue Demon, [[Mil Máscaras]], [[Tinieblas]], [[Rayo de Jalisco]], [[El Médico Asesino]], El Fantasma Blanco, El Avispon Escarlata and Superzan. In 1989, Blue Demon was the subject of a feature-length Mexican documentary entitled ''Blue Demon, the Champion'' (1989). ==Death== Muñoz died just before noon on Saturday, December 16, 2000.{{cite web|url=http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021117013853/http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 17, 2002|title=SLAM! Wrestling International -- 2000: The Year-In-Review Mexico|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=[[Canoe.com]]}} He suffered a fatal [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] on a park bench near a subway kiosk while on his way home from his regular morning training session at The ''Blue Demon Instituto Atletico'', where he was teaching others his fighting skills. Although an attempt was made to get him to a hospital, he was unable to be revived. He was 78 years old. Blue Demon was buried wearing his trademark blue mask, which was never removed in public as he always kept his true identity a secret. ==Legacy== Blue Demon is considered one of the biggest legends of ''lucha libre'' second only to El Santo in terms of popularity and influence both in and outside of Mexico. The distinctive blue and silver mask of Blue Demon and Blue Demon Jr. is known worldwide and is an instantly recognizable symbol of Lucha Libre. On Wikipedia, The mask icon is used as part of some professional wrestling related tags and notices.{{efn|Displayed above is the Wikipedia Icon featuring Blue Demon's mask.}} On October 27, 2000, CMLL held their first ever ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament in honor of Blue Demon.{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/blue.html#2000 | title= Leyenda de Azul 2000 | date= October 27, 2000 | access-date= June 11, 2010 | publisher= ProWrestlingHistory.com}}{{cite news | author = Box y Lucha staff | title = 2000 Especial! | work = Box y Lucha Magazine | pages= 2–20 | id = issue 2488 | date = January 9, 2001 | language = es}} The winner of the tournament receives a championship belt that features Blue Demon as well as a plaque with a Blue Demon mask on it. The tournament has been held on a semi-regular basis ever since, The tournament was first endorsed by Blue Demon Jr., and later endorsed by Muñoz' son. [[El Satánico]] |debut = {{dts|1995|10|18}} |retired = }} '''Renato Ruíz Cortes''' (born May 9, 1977), better known by his [[ring name]] '''Averno''' ([[English language|English]]: "[[Hades|Hell]]"), is a Mexican [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]]. He is signed to [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), where is a member of the ''[[Los Infernales]]'' stable and the current [[NWA World Historic Light Heavyweight Championship|NWA World Historic Light Heavyweight Champion]] in his first reign. He debuted for CMLL in 1995 as '''Rencor Latino''' ("Latin Hostility"), but did not achieve any significant success until adopting the ring name Averno in 2001 and joining ''Los Infernales''. A founding member of [[Los Hijos del Infierno|''Los Hijos del Averno'']] alongside [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Mephisto]] and [[Ephesto]], Averno was a one-time [[CMLL World Middleweight Championship|CMLL World Middleweight Champion]], [[NWA World Middleweight Championship|NWA World Middleweight Champion]], [[NWA World Historic Middleweight Championship|NWA World Historic Middleweight Champion]], [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship|Mexican National Welterweight Champion]] and [[Mexican National Trios Championship|Mexican National Trios Champion]], [[List of CMLL World Trios Champions|two-time]] [[CMLL World Trios Championship|CMLL World Trios Champion]], and [[List of CMLL World Tag Team Champions|three-time]] [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship|CMLL World Tag Team Champion]]. Ruíz left CMLL in April 2014 and joined rival promotion [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]] (AAA) the following month, where he was a one-time [[AAA World Tag Team Championship|AAA World Tag Team Champion]] and [[AAA World Trios Championship#Title history|three-time]] [[AAA World Trios Championship|AAA World Trios Champion]]. He left AAA in early 2021 and returned to CMLL that same year, where he has since won the [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship]] and the 2023 ''[[CMLL Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increíbles|Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increíbles]]'' with [[Místico]]. Averno has also wrestled for [[Total Nonstop Action Wrestling]] (TNA), where he won the [[2008 TNA World X Cup Tournament|2008 World X Cup]] as part of [[Team Mexico]], [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] (NJPW) and [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW). ==Personal life== Renato Ruíz Cortes was born on May 9, 1977, in [[Mexico City]].{{Cite web|title=Rudos – Averno|url=http://www.fuegoenelring.com/wrestlers_full_rudo.php?wrestlers_id=59|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711054029/http://www.fuegoenelring.com/wrestlers_full_rudo.php?wrestlers_id=59|archive-date=July 11, 2011|access-date=October 17, 2009|website=Fuego en el Ring|language=es}} The son of [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]] Rodolfo Ruíz, he began training for a professional wrestling career under his father, who by then had retired from in-ring competition and worked as a referee and trainer,{{Cite web|last=Rolando Marrón Vélez|first=Jorge|date=September 7, 2025|title=Muere Rodolfo Ruiz, histórico luchador y réferi del CMLL; padre de Averno y parte de una dinastía legendaria|url=https://www.clarosports.com/lucha-libre/fallece-rodolfo-ruiz-historico-luchador-y-referi-del-cmll-padre-de-averno-y-parte-de-una-dinastia-legendaria/|access-date=September 29, 2026|website=[[Claro Sports]]|language=es}} as well as [[El Satánico]], Felipe Ham Lee and [[Shadito Cruz]]. However, his father did not want him to become a wrestler and suggested he focus on his studies, intentionally making their training sessions brutal as a result; Ruíz recalled leaving the gym in tears two or three times.{{Cite web|last=Mojica|first=Rodrigo|date=November 9, 2022|title='Mi papá me cargaba la mano, me hacía llorar'; Averno la sufrió en su formación|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/cmll/averno-revela-su-padre-fue-duro-entrenamientos-ser-luchador-sin-mascaras|access-date=September 29, 2026|website=MedioTiempo|language=es}} == Professional wrestling career == === Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (1995–2014) === ==== Rencor Latino (1995–2001) ==== Ruíz made his in-ring debut on October 18, 1995, teaming with his father in a loss to [[Cassandro]] and Guerrero Star. Using the [[ring name]] Rencor Latino ("Latin Hostility"), he started out as a [[Face (professional wrestling)|''técnico'']] (good guy) in the lower ranks of [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), eventually winning his first ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' ("bet match") on June 19, 1998, by unmasking Apolo Chino following a midcard [[feud (professional wrestling)|feud]].{{cite news|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Rencor Latino|location=[[Mexico City]], [[Mexico]]|id=Tomo IV|pages=16|date=October 2007|language=es}} On February 27, 1999, he lost to Masato Yakushiji in a match to determine the inaugural [[CMLL World Lightweight Championship|CMLL Japan Super Lightweight Champion]].{{Cite book|last=Will|first=Gary|title=Wrestling Title Histories|last2=Duncan|first2=Royal|publisher=Archeus Communications|year=2000|isbn=0-9698161-5-4|page=388}} At the [[CMLL 66th Anniversary Show]] on September 24, Latino, [[Violencia]] and [[Virus (wrestler)|Virus]] lost to [[Starman (wrestler)|Starman]], Super Astro and [[Tony Rivera]].{{Cite web|date=September 24, 1999|title=66th Anniversary Show|url=https://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/anniversary75.html#66|access-date=September 19, 2008|publisher=ProWrestlingHistory.com}} On August 4, 2000, at the ''[[Entre Torre Infernal]]'' ("In the Infernal Tower") [[pay-per-view]], Latino defeated veteran [[Arturo Beristain|El Hijo del Gladiador]] in a ''Lucha de Apuestas'' to win his mask after being the final two wrestlers in a ''[[torneo cibernetico]]''. In early 2001, he underwent minor surgery on his left hand, but did not miss a significant amount of time out of the ring.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=February 2001|title=The Mexico Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=London Publishing Co.|page=91|issue=157|issn=1043-7576}} At [[Juicio Final (2001)|''Juicio Final'']] ("Final Judgement") on March 30, he, [[Arkangel de la Muerte]] and [[Veneno (wrestler)|Veneno]] lost to [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Astro Rey Jr.]], [[El Felino]] and [[Pantera (wrestler)|Pantera]].{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Mike|date=March 30, 2026|title=3/30 this day in history: Ric Flair loses retirement match at WrestleMania 24, WWF completes WCW purchase and more|url=https://www.pwinsider.com/article/92706/330-this-day-in-history-ric-flair-loses-retirement-match-at-wrestlemania-24-wwf-completes-wcw-purchase-and-more.html?p=1|access-date=September 30, 2026|website=Pro Wrestling Insider}} ==== ''Los Infernales'' (2001–2006) ==== {{main|Los Infernales}} [[File:Averno-CMLL.jpg|thumb|Ruíz wearing a half Averno/half Rencor Latino mask in 2005|317x317px]] In the summer of 2001, [[El Satánico]], who was feuding with former ''[[Los Infernales]]'' ("The Infernals") stablemates [[Último Guerrero]], [[Rey Bucanero]] and [[Toscano (wrestler)|Tarzan Boy]], recruited him to be a part of the new incarnation of ''Los Infernales'' and feud with the splinter group. During a televised segment, Satánico used his supposed "satanic powers" to turn Latino into one of his "minions", a [[Heel (professional wrestling)|''rúdo'']] (bad guy) character known as "Averno" ("Hell"), and Astro Rey Jr. into Mephisto. Ruíz' previous identity was publicly acknowledged, as he occasionally wrestled wearing a special half Averno and Rencor Latino mask.{{cite news|author=Enciclopedia staff|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Averno|location=[[Mexico City|Mexico City, Mexico]]|id=Tomo I|page=12|date=July 2007|language=es}}{{Cite news|date=January 13, 2002|title=2001 Especial!|work=[[Box y Lucha]]|pages=2–28|language=es|issue=2540}} When Tarzan Boy was injured and unable to wrestle, Bucanero and Guerrero recruited [[Antonio Gómez Medina|Máscara Mágica]] to even the numbers. The storyline between the two factions culminated when all seven wrestlers fought in a [[steel cage match]] at the [[CMLL 68th Anniversary Show]] on September 28, where the winning side would gain the rights to the ''Los Infernales'' name.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=July 2001|title=The Mexico Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=London Publishing Co.|page=75|issue=249|issn=1043-7576}} In the end, Satánico pinned Mágica to gain the rights and his mask. On June 23, 2002, ''Los Infernales'' won the [[Mexican National Trios Championship]] from [[Olímpico]], [[Mr. Niebla]] and [[Ephesto|Safari]], which they lost to ''La Familia de Tijuana'' ([[Psicosis|Nicho el Millonario]], [[Halloween (wrestler)|Halloween]] and [[Damián 666]]) on September 27. Shortly after, Averno and Mephisto [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Turn|turned]] on Satánico and split from the group, venturing out on their own.{{Cite news|date=January 5, 2004|title=Número Especial - Lo mejor de la lucha libre mexicana durante el 2003|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es|issue=240}} On September 3, 2004, Averno defeated [[Zumbido]] to win the vacant [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]]. On January 1, 2005, Averno lost the title to [[Místico]], from then on being positioned as his rival or [[Foil (narrative)|foil]]; their rivalry and matches received critical acclaim.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=October 2005|title=The International Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Kappa Publishing Group]]|page=56|issue=300|issn=1043-7576}}{{Cite web|last=Ocampo|first=Ernesto|date=January 7, 2007|title=Místico contra Averno: Déjà vu|url=https://superluchas.com/mistico-contra-averno-deja-vu/|access-date=July 9, 2009|website=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}} At [[Homenaje a Dos Leyendas (2005)|''Homenaje a Dos Leyendas'']] ("Homage to Two Legends") on March 18, Averno, Mephisto and Bucanero defeated [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]], [[Blue Panther]] and [[Negro Casas]].{{Cite news|last=Ocampo|first=Jorge|date=March 21, 2005|title=El Perro se va triunfante|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|pages=5–8|language=es|issue=101}} On April 1, Averno and Mephisto defeated Atlantis and Blue Panther to win the CMLL World Tag Team Championship. '''Richard Alan Baker''' (born December 8, 1950) is an American actor and retired [[Prosthetic makeup|special make-up effects]] creator.<ref name="filmref" /> He is mostly known for his creature designs and effects. Baker has won the [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Academy Award for Best Makeup]]<!--The award did not include hairstyling until 2012. Do not add it here as it was not called "hairstyling" at the time of Baker's nominations.--> a record seven times from a record eleven nominations, beginning with his win in the first year of the category's existence, for the 1981 [[comedy horror|horror comedy]] ''[[An American Werewolf in London]]''.<ref name="oscars">{{cite web |url=https://www.oscars.org/collection-highlights/rick-baker |title=Rick Baker |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=April 24, 2018}}</ref>

==Early life==
Baker was born on December 8, 1950, in [[Binghamton, New York]], to Doris ([[maiden and married names|née]] Hamlin), a bank teller, and Ralph B. Baker, a professional artist. He and his family moved to [[Covina, California]] when he was less than one year old.<ref name="filmref">{{cite web |url=http://www.filmreference.com/film/85/Rick-Baker.html |title=Rick Baker Biography (1950-) |publisher=Film Reference}}</ref><ref name="fatman">{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aSrNG1ctTKk |title=The Legendary Rick Baker! |date=September 24, 2019 |publisher=[[YouTube]] |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/aSrNG1ctTKk |archive-date=December 14, 2021 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Career==
As a teenager, Baker began creating artificial body parts in his own kitchen.{{citation needed|date=May 2012}} He also appeared briefly in the fan production ''The Night Turkey'', a one-hour, black-and-white video parody of ''[[The Night Stalker (1972 film)|The Night Stalker]]'' (1972), directed by [[William Malone (director)|William Malone]].{{citation needed|date=May 2012}} Among Baker's first professional jobs was assisting [[prosthetic makeup]] effects veteran [[Dick Smith (make-up artist)|Dick Smith]] on the 1973 film ''[[The Exorcist]]''.<ref name="oscars" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-dick-smith-20140801-story.html |title=Dick Smith dies at 92; 'Exorcist' makeup man won Oscar for 'Amadeus' |last=Nelson |first=Valerie J. |date=July 31, 2014 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref> While working on ''The Exorcist'', Baker was hired by director [[Larry Cohen]] to design and create a [[mutant]] infant for Cohen's 1974 film ''[[It's Alive (1974 film)|It's Alive]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Rick Baker: The Wonder Years Part Three |last=Martin |first=R. H. |date=August 1984 |magazine=[[Fangoria]] |publisher=[[Starlog|Starlog Group, Inc.]] |issue=37 |pages=31–32 |issn=0164-2111}}</ref>

At the [[54th Academy Awards]], Baker received the inaugural [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Academy Award for Best Makeup]]<!--The award did not include hairstyling until 2012. Do not add it here as it was not called "hairstyling" at that time or for Baker's later nominations.--> for his work on ''[[An American Werewolf in London]]'' (1981).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/makeup-artist-howard-j-smit-87280/ |title=Makeup artist Howard J. Smit dies |last=Barnes |first=Mike |date=August 4, 2009 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=August 12, 2009}}</ref> Subsequently, he has been nominated for Best Makeup ten more times, winning on seven occasions, both records in his field.  <ref name="oscars" /> His other Oscars came from ''[[Harry and the Hendersons]]'', ''[[Ed Wood (film)|Ed Wood]]'', ''[[The Nutty Professor (1996 film)|The Nutty Professor]]'', ''[[Men in Black (1997 film)|Men In Black]]'', ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000 film)|How The Grinch Stole Christmas]]'' and ''[[The Wolfman (film)|The Wolfman]]''.<ref name=oscarwinsandnominations>{{cite web|url=https://www.widescreenings.com/list-rick-baker-oscar-nominations.html|title=List of Rick Baker Oscar nominations, wins|publisher=widescreenings.com|accessdate=January 22, 2026}}</ref> Baker was also brought in by ''An American Werewolf in London'' [[John Landis]] to the music video ''[[Michael Jackson's Thriller (music video)|Thriller]]'' (1983), where Baker created the [[werecat]] creature [[Michael Jackson]] transforms into and multiple zombies that dance alongside Jackson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/editorials/3526115/came-80s-enduring-legacy-john-landis-rick-baker-michael-jacksons-thriller/ |title=[It Came From the '80s] The Enduring Legacy of John Landis, Rick Baker, and Michael Jackson's "Thriller" |last=Navarro |first=Meagan |date=October 29, 2018 |publisher=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Rick Baker at Saturn Awards (cropped).jpg|thumb|150px|Baker at the [[37th Saturn Awards]] in 2011]]

On November 30, 2012, Baker received the 2485th star of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]]. The star is located in front of the Guinness World Records Museum.<ref name="2485th">{{cite web |url=https://patch.com/california/hollywood/rick-baker-to-receive-walk-of-fame-star |title=Rick Baker to Receive Walk of Fame Star |last=Baguio |first=Lindsey |date=November 14, 2012 |publisher=Hollywood Patch |access-date=November 27, 2012}}</ref>

On May 28, 2015, Baker announced his retirement, saying: "First of all, the [[Computer-generated imagery|CG]] stuff definitely took away the animatronics part of what I do. It's also starting to take away the makeup part. The time is right, I am 64 years old, and the business is crazy right now. I like to do things right, and they wanted cheap and fast. That is not what I want to do, so I just decided it is basically time to get out. I would consider designing and consulting on something, but I don't think I will have a huge working studio anymore."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/2015/05/28/rick-baker-retires-auctions-collection/ |title=Rick Baker, special effects and make-up designer for 'Thriller,' to retire and auction off his collection |last=Dornbush |first=Jonathan |date=May 28, 2015 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=May 28, 2015 |archive-date=May 29, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529032807/http://www.ew.com/article/2015/05/28/rick-baker-retires-auctions-collection |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/make-up-legend-rick-baker-is-retiring/ |title=Make-Up Legend Rick Baker Is Retiring; Cites Studios Wanting "Cheap and Fast" Over Quality |last=Chitwood |first=Adam |date=May 28, 2015 |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=May 28, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/537876/rick-baker-retiring/ |title=Visual Effects Legend Rick Baker Is Retiring From Filmmaking |last=Fischer |first=Russ |date=May 28, 2015 |work=[[/Film]] |access-date=May 28, 2015}}</ref>

In 2018, when Baker's daughter Veronica was working at [[DC Comics]], he was approached by DC to design a collectible display bust. He agreed on the condition of total creative freedom; working with his long-time mold maker Rob Freitas, he created a bust of [[Joker (character)|The Joker]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Morrison |first=Matt |date=October 23, 2018 |title=Exclusive: How Rick Baker's the Joker Bust Was Crafted [Time-Lapse Video] |work=[[Screen Rant]] |url=https://screenrant.com/rick-baker-joker-bust/ |access-date=July 3, 2022}}</ref>

==Acting roles==
Baker played the [[King Kong|title role]] in the [[King Kong (1976 film)|1976 remake of ''King Kong'']]. He had initially only been hired to create an ape suit that would fill in for scenes where it was not practical to use a life-sized mechanical version of Kong that had been designed by [[Carlo Rambaldi]], but problems with Rambaldi's creation resulted in Baker playing Kong on-screen for almost all of the film.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/the-struggles-of-king-kong-76/ |title=The Struggles of King Kong '76 |last=Lambie |first=Ryan |date=March 10, 2017 |work=[[Den of Geek]] |access-date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> In the [[King Kong (2005 film)|2005 remake]], he had a cameo as the pilot and gunner (with director [[Peter Jackson]]) who shot down Kong. He has also made cameo appearances in: [[Michael Jackson]]'s music video ''[[Michael Jackson's Thriller (music video)|Thriller]]'' (1983) as "Zombie Opening the Crypt"; ''[[Into the Night (1985 film)|Into the Night]]'' (1985) as a drug dealer with a business card; ''[[Men in Black II]]'' (2002) as "MIB Passport Control Agent", an MIB agent helping provide aliens with disguises; ''[[Men in Black 3]]'' (2012) as "Brain Alien"; ''[[The Wolfman (2010 film)|The Wolfman]]'' (2010) as "Gypsy Man / First Killed"; [[The Strain (TV series)|''The Strain'']] as a convenience store customer (2014, Episode 8, uncredited) and ''[[Rings (2017 film)|Rings]]'' (2017) as a flea market vendor.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000711/#actor |title="Rick Baker - Actor Filmography" |publisher=[[IMDb]] |access-date=May 3, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Baker is married; he was previously married to Elaine Melba Parkyn for ten years. He met his second wife, hairstylist Silvia Abascal, while they were both working on ''[[Into the Night (1985 film)|Into the Night]]'' (1985).<ref name="fatman" /> Baker and Abascal had their first daughter 1989 and their second in 1993.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://werewolf-news.com/2018/10/rick-bakers-daughters-rebecca-and-veronica-become-a-new-american-werewolf-her-victim-for-halloween/ |title=Rick Baker's daughters Rebecca and Veronica become a new American Werewolf & her victim for Halloween |last=Quinton |first=Angela |date=October 31, 2018 |work=Werewolf News |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref>

'''Michael David Donovan''' (June 12, 1953 – March 4, 2026) was a Canadian voice actor and director.
== Career ==
Donovan had an extensive voiceover career in both western and Japanese animation. His voice roles include Wes Weasley in ''[[Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog]]'', [[Guile (Street Fighter)|Guile]] and [[Zangief]] in ''[[Street Fighter (TV series)|Street Fighter]]'', [[Eggplant Wizard]] in ''[[Captain N: The Game Master]]'', and [[Sabretooth (character)|Sabretooth]] in ''[[X-Men: Evolution]]''. His anime roles include [[Master Roshi]] in ''[[Dragon Ball (TV series)|Dragon Ball]]'', [[Ryoga Hibiki]] in ''[[Ranma ½]]'', and [[Cye Mouri]] and [[Sage Date]] in ''[[Ronin Warriors]]''.<ref name="Anime News Network">{{Cite web |last=Mateo |first=Alex |date=August 7, 2026 |title=SAG-AFTRA Lists Voice Actor Michael Donovan's Death |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2026-08-07/sag-aftra-lists-voice-actor-michael-donovan-death/.240382 |access-date=August 7, 2026 |website=[[Anime News Network]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Death ==
Donovan died on March 4, 2026, at the age of 72.<ref name="SAG-AFTRA Summer 2026 issue">{{Cite web |title=Summer 2026 magazine |url=https://digital.copcomm.com/i/1546062-summer-2026/79? |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=SAG-AFTRA}}</ref><ref name="Anime News Network" />

'''Julianna McCarthy''' is an American actress.

==Biography and career==
McCarthy began her career on the New York stage and appeared on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] in ''[[Inherit the Wind (play)|Inherit the Wind]]'' (1955–1957), alongside her husband, [[Michael Constantine]]. She and Constantine married on October 5, 1953; they had two children, Thea Eileen and Brendan Neil, before they divorced in 1972.<ref>Smith, Harrison. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/766212833/ Obituaries: Actor who starred in 'My Big Fat Greek Wedding']" (obituary of Michael Constantine). London, England: ''The Independent'', September 18, 2021, p. 44 (subscription required).</ref><ref>Fox, Margalit. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/952310556/ Michael Constantine, father in 'My Big Fat Greek Wedding']" (obituary of Michael Constantine). Buffalo, New York: ''The Buffalo News'', September 10, 2021, p. B5 (subscription required).</ref>

In 1986, she appeared on stage as the character Berte at the James A. Doolittle Theater in [[Hollywood, Los Angeles]] in the [[Mark Taper Forum]] production of ''[[Hedda Gabler]]'', which was directed by Robert Egan. Starring Egan's then-wife, [[Kate Mulgrew]], as Hedda, the production also included [[Linda Purl]] as Mrs. Elvsted.<ref>Kreiswirth, Sandra. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/607383651/ Taper's 'Hedda Gabler' has the look, lacks the fire]." Torrance, California: ''The Daily Breeze'', June 15, 1986, p. H7 (subscription required).</ref>

McCarthy was an original cast member of the [[soap opera]] ''[[The Young and the Restless]]'', starring as matriarch [[Liz Foster]] from 1973 to 1986.<ref>"[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1092811804/ News Q&A]." Portland, Oregon: ''The Oregonian'', May 28, 2013, p. A2 (subscription required).</ref> She reprised the role in 1993, 2003–2004,<ref>"[https://www.newspapers.com/image/270695970/ Soap Chat: Familiar faces are showing up]." Orlando, Florida: ''Orlando Sentinel'', January 5, 2003, p. X6 (subscription required).</ref> and 2008, returning for her most recent appearance in June 2010. While she was taken off of contract in late fall 1982{{Citation needed |date=August 2024}} and didn't make appearances for months, she was brought back on a recurring basis in time for the show's tenth anniversary, appearing semi-regularly for the next couple of years until her character moved to London. She was seen semi-regularly during the show's 30th anniversary when an ailing Liz revealed that her daughter, Jill, had been adopted. Her storyline concerned Jill's determination to find her birth parents. The character of Liz died in June 2010 on-screen.

McCarthy has also appeared in [[film|motion pictures]] including ''[[The Last American Virgin]]'', ''[[The Distinguished Gentleman]]'', ''[[The Frighteners]]'',<ref>"The Frighteners," in "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1064639151/ Movie of the Day]." Blackburn, Lancashire, England: ''Lancashire Telegraph'', p. M35 (subscription required).</ref> ''[[Starship Troopers (film)|Starship Troopers]]'' and ''[[Ted Bundy (film)|Ted Bundy]]''.<ref name=bfi/>

She had a recurring role as [[List of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine characters#Mila|Mila]] in ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', appearing in the episodes "[[Improbable Cause (DS9 episode)|Improbable Cause]]", "[[The Dogs of War (DS9 episode)|The Dogs of War]]" and the final episode, "[[What You Leave Behind (DS9 episode)|What You Leave Behind]]". McCarthy also had recurring roles in ''[[Paradise (American TV series)|Paradise]]'' and the 1991 remake of ''[[Dark Shadows (1991 TV series)|Dark Shadows]]'' as Mrs. Johnson, the housekeeper. In the show's flashbacks, she played the role of the calculating Collins relative Abigail.<ref>Novakovich, Lila. "Have you heard," in "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/734113557/ Soap Scene]." North Bay, Ontario, Canada: ''North Bay Nugget'', February 2, 1991, p. C6 (subscription required).</ref>
