'''Cherami Leigh Kuehn'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dualshockers.com/fortnite-fans-are-convinced-a-huge-marvel-actor-is-the-voice-of-paradigm/|title=Fortnite Fans are convinced a huge Marvel actor is the voice of Paradigm|last=Knight|first=Kyle|website=Dualshockers|date=June 6, 2022|access-date=February 16, 2025|archive-date=August 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824090106/https://www.dualshockers.com/fortnite-fans-are-convinced-a-huge-marvel-actor-is-the-voice-of-paradigm/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1023599760/ | title=18th annual Collin Theatre Center Award winners | newspaper=[[McKinney Courier-Gazette]] | date=May 27, 2010 | accessdate=February 16, 2025 | page=6A }}</ref> (born July 19, 1988)<ref name="Birthday">Birthday references:
* {{cite tweet|author=Funimation|user=Funimation_ANZ|number=1284646673755635712|title=Happy birthday to the amazingly talented Cherami Leigh!|date=July 19, 2020|access-date=February 17, 2025}}
* {{cite web|url=https://lionsbanebooking.com/project/cherami-leigh/|title=Cherami Leigh|publisher=Lionsbane Booking Agency|access-date=February 16, 2025}}</ref> is an American actress. She has provided voices for a number of English-language versions of [[anime]] series and video games.

==Early life and education==
Leigh began acting at the age of six.<ref name="resume"/> Leigh studied the [[Meisner technique]] with Nancy Chartier from the age of nine.<ref name="resume"/> As a child actress, she played Gretchen in ''[[Finding North]]'', Marcia in ''[[Temple Grandin (film)|Temple Grandin]]'', young [[LeAnn Rimes]] in ''[[Holiday in Your Heart]]'', Stacy Anderson in ''The President's Man'' and appeared on ''[[Walker, Texas Ranger]]'' multiple times.<ref name="resume"/>

She attended [[Hebron High School (Texas)|Hebron High School]] in Carrollton and studied theater at [[Collin College]], a public community college in [[Plano, Texas]].<ref name="resume"/>

==Career==
She also worked for [[Radio Disney]] as a DJ with voice-over promotions and commercials for [[ABC Radio (United States)|ABC Radio]] for 10 years.<ref name="resume"/> In 2013, she moved to [[Los Angeles]] where she continued voice-work and began taking on live-action roles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dallas.culturemap.com/news/entertainment/12-18-13-cry-movie-clay-luther-new-filmmakers-series-anthology-film-archives/#slide=0|title=Filmmaker packs debut feature with Dallas talent and takes on Big Apple|work=culturemap.com|date=December 18, 2013|access-date=February 14, 2017|archive-date=February 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170214184928/http://dallas.culturemap.com/news/entertainment/12-18-13-cry-movie-clay-luther-new-filmmakers-series-anthology-film-archives/#slide=0|url-status=live}}</ref>

Some of her roles include [[List of A Certain Magical Index characters#Sakugawa Middle School|Kazari Uiharu]] in ''[[A Certain Magical Index]]'' and ''[[A Certain Scientific Railgun]]'' series, [[List of Strike Witches characters#Yoshika Miyafuji|Yoshika Miyafuji]] in ''[[Strike Witches]]'', [[Is This a Zombie?#Eucliwood Hellscythe|Eucliwood Hellscythe]] in ''[[Is This a Zombie?]]'', [[Japanese destroyer Mutsuki|Mutsuki]] in ''[[Kantai Collection (TV series)|KanColle: Kantai Collection]]'', [[List of One Piece characters#Aisa|Aisa]] in ''[[One Piece (1999 TV series)|One Piece]]'', [[Mika Shimotsuki]] in ''[[Psycho-Pass]]'', Suzuha Amane in ''[[Steins;Gate]]'', [[List of Nabari no Ou characters#Shijima Kurookano|Shijima Kurookano]] in ''[[Nabari no Ou]]'', [[List of Sekirei characters#Hibiki|Hibiki]] in ''[[Sekirei]]'', [[List of Black Butler characters#Elizabeth Midford|Elizabeth Midford]] in ''[[Black Butler]]'', [[Road Kamelot]] in ''[[D.Gray-man]]'', [[Peach Girl#Sae Kashiwagi|Sae Kashiwagi]] in ''[[Peach Girl]]'', [[List of Bamboo Blade characters#Tamaki Kawazoe|Tamaki Kawazoe]] in ''[[Bamboo Blade]]'', [[List of Soul Eater characters#Liz and Patty Thompson|Patty Thompson]] in ''[[Soul Eater]]'', [[Lucy Heartfilia]] in ''[[Fairy Tail (TV series)|Fairy Tail]]'', [[The Sacred Blacksmith#Cecily Cambell|Cecily Campbell]] in ''[[The Sacred Blacksmith]]'', [[Asuna (Sword Art Online)|Asuna Yuuki]] in ''[[Sword Art Online (TV series)|Sword Art Online]]'', Kanono Ozu in ''[[Coppelion]]'', [[Sailor Venus]] in the Viz Media dub of ''[[Sailor Moon (TV series)|Sailor Moon]]'', [[List of Hyperdimension Neptunia characters#Plutia|Plutia / Iris Heart]] in ''[[Hyperdimension Neptunia]]'', [[Ulala (Space Channel 5)|Ulala]] in the ''[[Space Channel 5]]'' series, [[Sarada Uchiha]] in ''[[Boruto: Naruto Next Generations (TV series)|Boruto: Naruto Next Generations]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Con-Nichiwa – Cherami Leigh |url=http://www.con-nichiwa.com/item/14-cherami-leigh |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006213524/http://www.con-nichiwa.com/item/14-cherami-leigh |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |access-date=October 5, 2014 |work=Con-Nichiwa}}</ref> and [[List of RWBY characters#Menagerie Nation|Ilia Amitola]] in ''[[RWBY]]''.

On screen she has played a young [[LeAnn Rimes]] in ''[[Holiday in Your Heart]]'' and has appeared on ''[[Bones (TV series)|Bones]]'', ''[[Friday Night Lights (TV series)|Friday Night Lights]]'', ''[[Longmire (TV series)|Longmire]]'' and ''[[Shameless (American TV series)|Shameless]]''.

In video games, she voices Rottytops in the ''[[Shantae]]'' series, Gaige the Mechromancer in the ''[[Borderlands (series)|Borderlands]]'' series, Arianrhod in ''[[The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV]]'', Minerva in ''[[The Walking Dead: The Final Season]]'', Rhea in ''[[Fire Emblem: Three Houses]]'', [[List of Danganronpa characters#Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls|Komaru Naegi]] in ''[[Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls]]'', [[Makoto Niijima]] in ''[[Persona 5]]'', Cotton Cookie in Cookie Run: Kingdom, and the Female V in ''[[Cyberpunk 2077]]'' for which she was nominated for a [[British Academy Games Award for Performer in a Leading Role|BAFTA Award for Performer in a Leading Role]].

==Personal life==
Leigh married fellow actor Jon Christie on April 13, 2014, whom she had dated since 2010.<ref name="wedding post">{{cite web | url = https://www.facebook.com/beyondthemovie/photos/a.397306529732.172737.170290344732/10152232255189733/?type=1&theater | title = ★[CONGRATULATIONS!]★ Cherami Leigh (Anne Wells) and Jon Christie just tied the knot! | work = Facebook | author = Beyond the Farthest Star | author-link = Beyond the Farthest Star (film) | date = April 15, 2014 | access-date = October 13, 2014 | archive-date = June 7, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210607114204/https://www.facebook.com/beyondthemovie/photos/a.397306529732.172737.170290344732/10152232255189733/?type=1&theater | url-status = live }}</ref> They have one daughter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 October 2023 |title=Happy Halloween! |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CzE_cgYSoJu/?igshid=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |website=Instagram |access-date=October 31, 2023 |archive-date=October 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031212841/https://www.instagram.com/p/CzE_cgYSoJu/?igshid=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |url-status=live }}</ref>

Pepe Mendieta | debut = {{dts|1985|7|11}} | retired = | family = [[Blue Demon]] (adoptive father) }} '''Blue Demon Jr.''' (born July 19, 1966) is a Mexican [[professional wrestler]]. He is the adopted son of the original [[Blue Demon]] and is the first Mexican and second masked wrestler to win the [[NWA World Heavyweight Championship]] thus making him a one-time [[Professional wrestling championship#World championships|world champion]]. His government name has never been officially disclosed to the public, as is often the case with masked wrestlers in Mexico where their on-stage personas are kept separate from their personal lives.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha Libre: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Okay... what is Lucha Libre?|pages=29–40|isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} ==Professional wrestling career== ===United Wrestling Association (1984–1989)=== ===CMLL (1989–1995)=== ===Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (1996–2001)=== In [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]] (AAA) he formed the team ''Los Juniors'' with [[La Parka (AAA)|La Parka Jr.]], Mascara Sagrada Jr. and [[Perro Aguayo Jr.]] On April 18, 1999, in [[Zapopan, Jalisco]] they won the [[Mexican National Atómicos Championship]] by defeating ''Los Vatos Locos'', a team of [[Charly Manson]], May Flowers, [[Nygma (wrestler)|Nygma]] and Picudo. On September 17, 1999, in [[Mexico City|Mexico City, D.F.]] they lost the championship to ''[[Los Vipers]]'', a team of [[Histeria (wrestler)|Histeria]], [[Maniaco]], [[Mosco de la Merced II]] and [[Psicosis II]]. ===National Wrestling Alliance (2008–2010)=== [[File:El Hijo De Santo vs Blue Demon Jr.jpg|right|thumb|200 px|Blue Demon Jr. (behind, in blue costume) versus [[El Hijo del Santo]]]] On October 25, 2008, Demon Jr. became the first Mexican professional wrestler, as well as first masked luchador to win the [[NWA World Heavyweight Championship]] when he defeated champion [[Adam Pearce]]. His win was also the first time the title changed hands in [[Mexico]], although not with [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre|CMLL]] as would have been the case before the mid-1980s (It happened in Blue Demon Jr.'s own promotion: NWA Mexico). Pearce protested the loss with the NWA as his arm was under the bottom rope when he passed out from Blue Demon Jr's [[Boston crab#Single leg Boston crab|Single leg Boston crab]]. Blue Demon Jr. managed to hold on to the championship for 505 days before dropping it back to Pearce in a triple-threat match also involving [[Phill Shatter]] on March 14, 2010, at NWA New Beginnings.{{cite web|url=https://pwinsider.com/article/45909/new-nwa-champion-crowned.html?p=1| title=New NWA Champion crowned|access-date=2010-03-14|publisher=Pro Wrestling Insider}} ===Pro Wrestling Revolution (2010–2013)=== Demon Jr. defeated Oliver John at an NWA Mexico event at the Lucha Libre Expo in Mexico City on July 23, 2010, to capture the Pro Wrestling Revolution (PWR) Heavyweight Championship. On May 11, 2013, [[El Hijo del Santo]] and his rival, Blue Demon Jr., joined forces to win the Pro Wrestling Revolution Tag Team Championship after defeating [[Brian Cage]] and [[Derek Sanders]]{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/elhijodelsanto-y-bluedemonjr-son-los-nuevos-campeones-en-pareja-de-pwrrevolution/|title=¡@ElHijodelSanto y @BlueDemonjr son los Nuevos Campeones en Pareja de @PWRevolution!|first=William|last=Beltrán|date=May 12, 2013}} On September 6, 2012, Blue Demon Jr. lost the PWR World Heavyweight Championship to [[Carly Colón]] in a match that also involved [[La Parka II]]. On November 13, 2013, Blue Demon Jr. disbanded NWA Mexico and became officially affiliated with PWR.{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestling-revolution.com/2013/11/13/pro-wrestling-revolution-welcomes-new-partner/|title=Pro Wrestling Revolution welcomes new partner|date=2013-11-13|access-date=2013-11-14|work=Pro Wrestling Revolution|archive-date=September 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915225829/http://www.prowrestling-revolution.com/2013/11/13/pro-wrestling-revolution-welcomes-new-partner/|url-status=dead}} ===Lucha Underground (2014–2015)=== In August 2014, Blue Demon Jr. was announced as one of five AAA wrestlers to star in the [[El Rey (network)|El Rey]] network's new television series ''[[Lucha Underground]]''.{{cite web | url = http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/38664-el-rey-network-announces-more-details-of-aaa-lucha-libre-project | title = El Rey Network announces more details of AAA Lucha Libre project | date = August 27, 2014 | access-date = August 28, 2014 | work = [[Dave Meltzer#Wrestling Observer Newsletter|Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140905015135/http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/38664-el-rey-network-announces-more-details-of-aaa-lucha-libre-project | archive-date = September 5, 2014 }} Blue Demon Jr. wrestled in the first match of the debut episode of ''Lucha Underground'' on October 29, defeating [[Chavo Guerrero Jr.]]{{cite web|last1=Peeples|first1=Jeremy|title=Lucha Underground TV report: Prince Puma (Ricochet) vs. Johnny Mundo (John Morrison)|url=http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/39646|publisher=Wrestling Observer|access-date=November 2, 2014|date=October 29, 2014}} In the LU storyline, Blue Demon Jr. was hospitalized due to vicious after-match attacks by both Mil Muertes and Chavo Guerrero Jr. following Demon's loss to Mil Muertes in the November 5 main event match. Upon his return, he attacked Chavo and later in a face-to-face meeting with Chavo blocked another attack and emerged triumphant after laying Chavo out. On July 8, 2015, Demon turned ''rudo'' attacking Texano Jr. ===Return to AAA (2013–present)=== Blue Demon Jr. returned to AAA on March 3, 2013, challenging [[El Texano Jr.]] to a match for the [[AAA Mega Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/confirmado-bluedemonjr-vs-texano-jr-por-el-megacampeonato-aaa-en-rey-de-reyes-2013/|title=Confirmado: @BlueDemonjr vs. Texano Jr. por el MegaCampeonato AAA en Rey de Reyes 2013|last=Beltrán|first=William|date=March 3, 2013|access-date=March 4, 2013|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}} The match took place on March 17 at ''[[Rey de Reyes (2013)|Rey de Reyes]]'' and saw El Texano Jr. retain his title. [[California Institute of the Arts]] | occupation = Puppeteer | years_active = 1974–present }} '''Allan Trautman''' (born May 25, 1955) is an American [[puppeteer]], best known for his work with [[The Jim Henson Company]]. ==Early life== He is originally from [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. Trautman has a B.A. in Physics and Drama from [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]].{{Cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Denise |date=November 3, 1997 |title=Puppeteer Pulls Strings of His Future |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-nov-03-fi-49843-story.html |access-date= |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}} He later obtained an MFA in Acting from the [[California Institute of the Arts]] in 1978.{{Cite web |last=Lotze |first=Katharine |date=September 27, 2016 |title=Talking with his hands |url=https://signalscv.com/2016/09/talking-with-his-hands/ |access-date= |website=Santa Clarita Valley Signal |language=en-US}} ==Career== He had his first job as a puppeteer during college working on [[The Letter People]]. Trautman spent two summers performing at the [[Colorado Shakespeare Festival]].{{cite journal|last=Turner|first=Jerry|title=Colorado Shakespeare Festival|journal=Shakespeare Quarterly|date=Summer 1980|volume=31|issue=2|pages=249–251|jstor=2869549|doi=10.2307/2869549}}{{cite journal|last=Wickstrom|first=Gordon|title=Colorado Shakespeare Festival|journal=Shakespeare Quarterly|date=Spring 1979|volume=30|issue=2|pages=226–229|jstor=2869315|doi=10.2307/2869315}} He stayed in Los Angeles after graduation and performed with [[Sid and Marty Krofft]]. In 1985, he portrayed The Tarman, one of the lead zombies of the "Return of The Living Dead" film series, often considered one of the most iconic zombies in film. He would return to the role for two of the film's sequels in 1986 and 2005, respectively. Trautman began working with the Muppets in 1990 on ''[[Muppet*Vision 3D]]'', which played at [[Disney's Hollywood Studios]] from 1991 to 2025, and [[Disney California Adventure]] from 2001 to 2014.
